findings.summary: knn_aggregate's docstring promises automatic self-match exclusion ('query is ref is leak-safe by construction') but the non-group-filtered code path never removes a distance-0 self-match, only truncates to the first k of k+1 neighbours.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly detect and drop a same-row self-match (or require a row-identity group id) before truncating to k, in both the plain and group-filtered branches.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call knn_aggregate(coords, coords, labels, k=k) with query is ref and no group_ids; assert no row's own label contributes to its own neighbour aggregate. Generalize to any kNN/radius aggregator whose docstring claims query-is-ref leak-safety.

findings.summary: make_focal_objective's LightGBM focal-loss gradient/hessian formula is mathematically wrong (verified numerically via finite differences and symbolically via sympy against the loss the code itself computes) -- corrupts every model trained through focal_lgb.py and multi_aux_ensemble.py's focal=True path.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with the closed-form binary focal-loss gradient/Hessian (y=1: grad = gamma*p*(1-p)^gamma*log(p) - (1-p)^(gamma+1); y=0 mirror) and verify with a numerical-gradient-check test.
findings.meta_test_idea: Generic custom-objective gradient checker: for every (preds, train_data)->(grad,hess) LightGBM/XGBoost objective closure in the repo, assert returned grad/hess match finite-difference/sympy derivatives of the claimed loss to ~1e-4.

findings.summary: apply_nan_in_X_policy's default 'impute' path crashes (ValueError: could not convert string to float) on any object/category/string-dtype column containing NaN, when the configured core estimator(s) don't all natively tolerate NaN -- defeating the module's own documented 'graceful median-impute so RFECV no longer hard-crashes on NaN' contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the impute loop on is_numeric_dtype/is_bool_dtype; skip (or mode-impute) non-numeric columns instead of blindly casting via to_numpy(dtype=float).
findings.meta_test_idea: Fuzz RFECV.fit with mixed-dtype X (object/category column with NaN) across estimator families (linear, sklearn RandomForest, CatBoost) under nan_in_X_policy='impute' and assert no crash.

findings.summary: show_calibration_plot(backend="plotly", show_plots=False) raises UnboundLocalError on 'fig' (confirmed live) because `fig` is only assigned inside the matplotlib branch but returned unconditionally.
findings.suggested_fix: Initialize fig=None at function top, or raise a clear ValueError for the unsupported parameter combination.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST/CFG def-before-use checker: flag any local read on a path where no preceding assignment dominates it, across all multi-branch functions.

findings.summary: maximum_absolute_percentage_error crashes with ValueError on empty y_true/y_pred (np.nanmax on zero-size array) instead of returning NaN like every sibling metric in the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same `if len(y_true)==0: return NaN` guard used by every sibling wrapper in this module.
findings.meta_test_idea: Parametrized sweep calling every exported metric function with empty arrays; assert NaN or a documented ValueError, never an undocumented exception.

findings.summary: fast_concordance_index computes (kendall_tau_b+1)/2, which only equals the true Harrell C-index when there are zero ties; with tied predictions (common for tree-ensemble risk scores) it is systematically wrong (verified: 0.9082 vs correct 0.8333 on a minimal example).
findings.suggested_fix: Implement the direct pairwise C-index definition (exclude only y_true-tied pairs, credit y_pred-tied pairs with 0.5), not tau-b's symmetric tie discount.
findings.meta_test_idea: Property test comparing fast_concordance_index against a brute-force independent C-index reference on data with deliberately duplicated prediction values, not just tie-free noise.

findings.summary: augment_temporal_drift's expanding mean/std uses the catastrophic-cancellation-prone sum(x^2)-(sum(x))^2/n formula; on realistic large-offset/small-spread columns this goes negative, gets clipped to 0, and the augmented z-scored feature silently collapses to a constant 0.0 for every synthetic row (empirically reproduced: offset=1e9, scale=0.5 -> negative variance for 6/7 windows vs. a stable two-pass reference).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a numerically stable two-pass or Welford-style expanding variance, mirroring the _centered_moments_njit pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase for the identical bug class (e.g. _binned_numeric_agg_fe.py's _global_stats_all fix).
findings.meta_test_idea: AST/grep scanner flagging cumsum(x**2) - cumsum(x)**2/n -shaped expressions repo-wide; a property test asserting expanding/rolling variance matches pd.Series.expanding().var() within tolerance across offset/scale sweeps (offset up to 1e9, scale down to 1e-1).

findings.summary: select_column_transforms computes every non-identity candidate transform (all sklearn scalers, RankGauss, and the NaN-median fill) on the WHOLE column before the K-fold CV split, then scores it per fold on that pre-computed array, so the 'honest' CV score is optimistically biased for every candidate except identity/log1p_signed (confirmed: a scaler fit on the whole column vs. fit only on a train subset produces different stats on the held-out test subset).
findings.suggested_fix: Move _apply_transform for cross-row-statistic candidates inside the fold loop, fitting only on train_idx and transforming test_idx with those train-only stats, mirroring gaussian_power_transform_search's correct fit/apply split.
findings.meta_test_idea: Synthetic column where identity is genuinely optimal: assert the leaky pre-split CV score for StandardScaler/RankGauss does not exceed an honest per-fold-refit score by more than noise; scanner flagging a .fit/.fit_transform call outside a CV fold loop whose output is later indexed by both train_idx and test_idx of that loop.

findings.summary: analyse_and_clean_features's nunique==2 replacement branch only assigns repl_value for isinstance(real_val,str), col_is_numeric, or col_is_boolean with no final else, so a 2-valued categorical column whose real value is none of those (e.g. decimal.Decimal, pd.Timestamp) raises UnboundLocalError; reproduced live with a Categorical column holding one Decimal value plus None.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an else branch (e.g. a generic 'not <real_val>' repl_value, or leave the NaN unmapped with a logged warning) instead of relying on exactly three type checks being exhaustive.
findings.meta_test_idea: Fuzz test feeding analyse_and_clean_features 2-valued object/category columns across a matrix of Python value types (str, int, float, bool, Decimal, Timestamp, tuple, custom object) asserting no UnboundLocalError.

findings.summary: predict_mlframe_models_suite (disk-loading predict entry point) lacks the CTE-RAW-X routing, the value-transform re-raise safety net, and the text/embedding passthrough that its sibling predict_from_models has via the shared _apply_pre_pipeline_with_passthrough helper -- composite-target (CompositeTargetEstimator) models loaded from disk silently predict in the wrong (residual/T) scale, with no error raised.
findings.suggested_fix: Route the suite path's per-model pre_pipeline application through the shared _apply_pre_pipeline_with_passthrough helper (threading a df_pre_pipeline snapshot like predict_from_models does) and add the same CompositeTargetEstimator raw-frame routing at the _predict_with_fallback call sites.
findings.meta_test_idea: Parity test: train a composite-target suite, save to disk, and assert predict_from_models and predict_mlframe_models_suite produce matching, correctly-y-scaled predictions on the same frame. Generalized: a sibling-predict-entry-point drift scanner diffing which shared safety helpers each public predict function calls vs. reimplements inline.

findings.summary: partial_fit re-factorizes categorical columns from scratch on every incremental call, desyncing the frozen CategoricalEmbedding table's code assignment from batch to batch.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate _factorize_cats_fit / _encode_emb_text_fit on is_partial_fit and reuse self._cat_code_maps_ / self._emb_text_encoder_ from the first call, mirroring the label-encoder's own is_partial_fit reuse branch a few lines above in base/_base_fit.py.
findings.meta_test_idea: Scanner: flag any _fit_common-style method receiving an is_partial_fit flag that calls a *_fit(...) helper unconditionally while a sibling helper in the same function IS gated on that flag.

findings.summary: _apply_cat_codes maps a categorical column via .map(code_maps[col]) without casting to object first; on pandas Categorical dtype this crashes on .fillna(card) trying to add a new category -- the exact bug already fixed in the sibling flat-MLP implementation but never ported here.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same .astype(object) cast used in base/_base_fit_prep.py:133 before .map(...).
findings.meta_test_idea: Fit RecurrentClassifierWrapper/RecurrentRegressorWrapper with a pandas.Categorical-dtype cat_features column with an unseen value in eval_set/predict; grep scanner for .map(...code_maps/mapping...) sites lacking a preceding .astype(object).

findings.summary: attach_new_columns() joins new feature columns onto train/val/test by pandas index LABEL (df.join), but 6 of the 8 composite-FE sibling modules build the new-columns frame with a fresh RangeIndex(0..n-1) while the caller's df carries the original non-contiguous row-index left over from the upstream df.iloc[train_idx] split. The join silently produces NaN or cross-row-misattributed feature values for most rows on any pandas-backed run.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix once in attach_new_columns(): re-index new_cols onto df.index positionally before the join/concat (e.g. new_cols.set_axis(df.index, axis=0) when lengths match), so all 6 call sites are fixed without touching them individually. Alternatively require every caller to build new_cols with index=df.index (the pattern _categorical_composite_fe.py already uses correctly) and assert inside attach_new_columns that the indices are compatible.
findings.meta_test_idea: Property test: call attach_new_columns(df, new_cols) with a pandas df carrying a shuffled/non-default index and new_cols built with a fresh RangeIndex; assert output equals row-order-based expectation, not label-based. Generalize as an AST/grep scanner flagging pd.DataFrame(..., index=range(...)) / .reset_index(drop=True) results later passed into a .join()/pd.concat(axis=1) against a differently-indexed frame.

findings.summary: EmbeddingProvider overrides __repr__ to scrub api_key/token/secret params but never overrides __str__, so str()/f-strings/%s-logging print the raw unscrubbed secret (verified live with a real credential value).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `__str__ = __repr__` (or an explicit scrubbed __str__) next to the existing __repr__ override.
findings.meta_test_idea: For every class that scrubs secrets inside __repr__, assert __str__ is aliased/overridden identically; or a property test constructing a canary-secret instance and asserting the canary is absent from repr(x), str(x), f"{x}", and "%s" % x.

findings.summary: replay_cv_results(fname, trusted_root=None) only enforces the joblib.load path-containment check when trusted_root is explicitly passed, unlike every sibling joblib.load call site in the codebase which fails closed by default; neither the sole production caller nor the sole test passes trusted_root, so the containment check never runs today.
findings.suggested_fix: Make trusted_root mandatory (raise ValueError when None, matching training/_data_helpers.py._validate_trusted_path) or default it to the file's own parent directory the way training/_trainer_train_and_evaluate.py already does.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST-grep every function calling joblib.load/dill.load/pickle.load and assert the load is unreachable unless a shared trusted-root validator ran unconditionally on that code path (not inside an `if trusted_root is not None:` guard).

findings.summary: _canonical_group_key_series stringifies a genuine None/NaN group label to the literal string "None"/"nan" for non-floating (object/string) dtype arrays instead of preserving it as missing, so it silently becomes a real fitted group instead of being excluded, contradicting the function's own docstring and its own logged warning.
findings.suggested_fix: In the non-floating branch, detect pd.isna per element the same way the floating branch does and leave those positions as actual np.nan (not str(None)) before constructing the pd.Series.
findings.meta_test_idea: For every group-bearing fit_*/apply_* pair, build an object-dtype group array containing None/np.nan and assert pd.isna(canonical) == pd.isna(original), and that the fitted table never contains a "nan"/"None" key.

findings.summary: _bootstrap_ece_with_indices's fused idx-aware bootstrap loop (used whenever n_bins is passed, i.e. always from pick_best_calibrator) feeds the njit kernel raw un-normalized y_true labels while the point estimate two lines above normalizes them via _normalize_binary_labels, so for non-{0,1}-encoded labels the bootstrap CI is computed on a different scale than the point estimate it should bracket.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize y_true via _normalize_binary_labels before building yb in the n_bins-is-not-None branch, mirroring _ece_score's own normalization.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call pick_best_calibrator(..., selection="same_oof") with oof_y encoded as {-1,+1} vs {0,1} on the same underlying data and assert the reported ece_ci matches between encodings.

findings.summary: assert_no_group_leakage never materializes cv_splits to a list despite its own docstring promising exactly that ('consumed eagerly... without exhausting it for the caller'); passing a real generator silently exhausts it, so a downstream CV loop reusing the same generator silently runs zero folds.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `cv_splits = list(cv_splits)` at the top of the function, matching the documented contract.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep every docstring phrase 'materialized to a list'/'consumed eagerly'/'without exhausting' and assert the corresponding parameter is wrapped in list(...)/tuple(...) before the first iteration in the function body.

findings.summary: evaluate_estimators's classification_thresholds: Optional[list] param is used incompatibly across branches: .map() (needs dict-like) for classifiers vs. np.asarray() (needs array-like) for regressors; passing the documented list type to a classifier crashes with TypeError: 'list' object is not callable (reproduced end-to-end with a real LogisticRegression).
findings.suggested_fix: Split into two differently-named/typed parameters, or coerce consistently (e.g. accept only a dict and derive the bin-edge array from sorted(dict.values()) for the regressor path).
findings.meta_test_idea: AST scanner: flag any single function parameter passed both to pandas.Series.map() and to np.asarray()/used as a numeric array in different branches of the same function.

findings.summary: detect_expanding_window_feature_leakage's leaky_row_ranges collapses each fold's leaked original-df positions to (min, max+1), which is only a valid contiguous range when df was already time-sorted; on unsorted input (the realistic case, since the function sorts internally) it reports a range spanning nearly the entire dataset instead of the actual leaked rows, contradicting the docstring's 'exact rows' claim (reproduced: 200-row fixture, every fold's reported range spans ~190-200 of 200 rows).
findings.suggested_fix: Return the actual (possibly non-contiguous) sorted np.ndarray of original positions instead of a (start, end) envelope, or detect the unsorted case and fall back to an explicit index list.
findings.meta_test_idea: Property test: shuffle original row order relative to time_col, run with auto_remediate=True, and assert each reported range's width stays within a small constant factor of the true per-fold row count.

findings.summary: scan_temporal_leak's _rank_columns skips tie-averaging, yet split_labels is documented as possibly 'a binary train=0/test=1 indicator' (maximal tie density, the module's primary use case); reproduced a ~0.13 absolute (~15% relative) systematic inflation vs. scipy.stats.spearmanr's tie-aware result (0.996 vs 0.865) on an identical leaky-feature fixture with binary split_labels.
findings.suggested_fix: Use scipy.stats.rankdata(method='average') (or an equivalent midrank scatter) when split_labels cardinality is low relative to n, or narrow the docstring's claimed use case to genuinely continuous split labels.
findings.meta_test_idea: Differential property test: compare every custom rank-correlation helper against scipy.stats.spearmanr on a heavily-tied (<=5 distinct values) fixture, asserting divergence stays under a fixed tolerance.

findings.summary: compute_numerical_aggregates_numba silently returns a wrong-length list for empty (or recursively-degenerate) input, breaking the documented fixed-width contract with get_basic_feature_names()
findings.suggested_fix: Route the size==0 fast path (and the drawdown/duration recursive sub-calls when a sub-array collapses to length 0) through a NaN-filled vector whose length matches the caller's requested flags, not a hardcoded [0.0]
findings.meta_test_idea: Property test: for every flag combination and n in {0,1,2,3}, assert len(compute_numerical_aggregates_numba(arr, **kw)) == len(get_basic_feature_names(**kw))

findings.summary: per_group_rolling_reduce crashes with ValueError for op in {std,var,median,min,max} whenever min_periods < window_K and a group's length falls in [min_periods, window_K)
findings.suggested_fix: Give the std/var/median/min/max branch the same partial-window handling sum/mean already has, or clamp/mask sliding_window_view's window instead of letting it raise
findings.meta_test_idea: Parametrized test: for every op, sweep seg_len from min_periods to window_K-1 and assert no exception / correct output length

findings.summary: binned_unique_count crashes with ValueError ('bincount... non-negative') whenever entity_col contains any NaN/missing label alongside a valid value_col observation, because pd.factorize's -1 sentinel flows unmasked into np.bincount
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude rows whose entity_codes == -1 before building combined_key (mirroring how `valid` already excludes non-finite value_col), or raise an explicit ValueError up front
findings.meta_test_idea: Fuzz test injecting a NaN/None into entity_col on a row with a finite value_col; assert no crash and documented handling

findings.summary: bocpd_features has no validation on NIG prior hyperparameters (kappa0/alpha0/beta0); alpha0=0.0 crashes with an unhandled ZeroDivisionError from inside the njit kernel, and the sibling online_bayesian_linear_regression silently returns all-NaN output for prior_precision<=0 with no warning
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit upfront positivity check raising ValueError for kappa0/alpha0/beta0 and prior_precision/noise_sigma
findings.meta_test_idea: Unit test: call each Bayesian entry point with each positivity-constrained kwarg set to 0.0 and -1.0; assert a clean ValueError, not an internal exception or silent NaN

findings.summary: add_anchor_extrapolation_features (the module's primary/flagship function) has no numba-accelerated path, unlike all four sibling functions in the same file which were explicitly converted from Python list append/pop to preallocated njit buffers
findings.suggested_fix: Add an njit core for the anchor rolling-slope recursion mirroring the pattern already used 4x in this file, dispatched when numba is available
findings.meta_test_idea: Perf regression test comparing add_anchor_extrapolation_features wall-time at n=200k against a sibling njit-accelerated anchor function on equivalent data

findings.summary: _hurst_rs_single's docstring claims 'Same definition as compute_hurst_rs' but uses x.std() (ddof=0) while compute_hurst_rs explicitly uses ddof=1 sample std, a real formula divergence (~2.6% bias at K=20) between the rolling and multi-scale Hurst feature families.
findings.suggested_fix: Match ddof=1 in _hurst_rs_single, or correct the docstring to document the intentional difference and its magnitude.
findings.meta_test_idea: Scanner: flag function pairs whose docstrings assert 'same definition/formula as X' but whose std/var calls use different explicit ddof values.

findings.summary: Module docstring promises chunk-bounded peak memory, but pruning now happens up-front for ALL pairs via a covariance matrix and every surviving pair's diff column is accumulated into one dict before returning -- chunk_size no longer bounds peak memory, so a low variance threshold with many columns can still blow up to O(C(n_cols,2)*n_rows).
findings.suggested_fix: Either flush/yield each chunk's surviving columns incrementally, or update the docstring to state the real (non-chunk-bounded) memory contract.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep for 'streams/chunks to bound memory' docstring claims and confirm the implementation actually flushes/yields per chunk rather than accumulating everything before returning.

findings.summary: knn_gradient_features wraps a batched np.linalg.solve for ALL query rows in one try/except LinAlgError; one singular neighbourhood (e.g. duplicate/quantized coordinates) sets gradient features to NaN for the ENTIRE batch, not just the offending row.
findings.suggested_fix: Fall back per-row (lstsq or a loop) only for the rows that actually fail, instead of nulling the whole batch on any single failure.
findings.meta_test_idea: Inject one duplicated-coordinate (rank-deficient) neighbourhood into an otherwise well-conditioned batch; assert only that row's output is NaN.

findings.summary: create_windowed_features's insufficient-window skip-guard is asymmetric: without targets_creation_fcn it checks an exact expected-window count, but with targets_creation_fcn set it only checks non-emptiness of future_windows_features, so a partially-satisfied future window set silently proceeds instead of being skipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same exact expected-vs-actual window count check in both dispatch modes.
findings.meta_test_idea: Request 2 future windows where only 1 hits the data boundary with targets_creation_fcn set; assert the row is skipped like the no-targets_creation_fcn path.

findings.summary: Windowed sum/mean features are computed as the difference of two independently-computed CUMULATIVE aggregates (upper - lower); when history span greatly exceeds the horizon, this subtracts two large nearly-equal numbers, risking catastrophic cancellation -- the same bug class this codebase has repeatedly fixed elsewhere in subtractive derivations.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the windowed sum directly (not via cumulative-minus-cumulative) for large-history entities, or document/guard the precision risk.
findings.meta_test_idea: Entity with a huge historical cumulative sum and a small windowed delta; assert the windowed sum/mean matches a direct (non-subtractive) computation to tight tolerance.

findings.summary: Band/anchor assignment uses in-sample baseline predictions (fit-then-predict on the same rows) to rank row hardness/disagreement, biasing which rows become anchors; sibling file bidir_residual_band.py already diagnosed and fixed this exact issue via inner-KFold OOF but the fix wasn't propagated here (also affects class_balanced_hard_row.py and fisher_weighted_residual.py in this cluster).
findings.suggested_fix: Route the baseline fit through the same inner-KFold(3) OOF helper pattern bidir_residual_band.py / baseline_surprise.py / decision_region_depth.py already implement.
findings.meta_test_idea: Scan for fit-then-predict-on-same-array patterns inside functions whose docstring mentions residual/hardness/disagreement/band; cross-reference against sibling files in the same directory that already solved it via OOF.

findings.summary: Naive Xq_s[:, None, :] - anchors[None, :, :] broadcast materializes an (n_query, n_anchors, d) cube instead of using the GEMM-decomposition squared_dists helper already used by sibling files anchor_attention.py / class_conditional_anchor.py in the same package; recurs in bidir_residual_band.py:151, class_balanced_hard_row.py:162, disagreement_band.py:151 -- real OOM risk at the codebase's documented 100+GB / d<=32768 production scale.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the broadcast-cube pattern in all 4 files with _squared_dists_shared.squared_dists(Xq_s, anchors), matching anchor_attention.py/class_conditional_anchor.py.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST/grep scanner flagging the literal [:, None, :] - ... [None, :, :] pattern anywhere under feature_engineering/, requiring use of squared_dists or an explicit size-bounded justification.

findings.summary: Per-row numerical-stability shift applied to the key-side (training) Performer random features silently reweights each training row's contribution to the linear-attention aggregate by an arbitrary factor, corrupting the kernel approximation.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a single GLOBAL scalar stabilization shift for phi_k (not per-row axis=1 max) so it cancels uniformly out of A/B; keep the existing per-row shift for phi_q, which is provably harmless there.
findings.meta_test_idea: Compare Performer y_estimate against brute-force softmax-exact attention on a small synthetic dataset across n_features; generic scanner for per-row max-stabilization applied to an array later reduced via sum/matmul across the same row axis.

findings.summary: The documented 'quantile-loss LightGBM' third aux model for regression is never implemented; _fit_aux_lgb's focal=True branch only special-cases task=='binary', so the regression 'focal' model is a near-duplicate of the first aux model (same hyperparams, seed+1), silently weakening the disagreement feature.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement the documented quantile-objective LGBMRegressor branch for focal=True + task=='regression', or correct the docstring/column semantics.
findings.meta_test_idea: Assert m_focal's fitted structure/objective differs from m_lgb's beyond random_state for task='regression'; scanner for flavor-flag guards with no matching branch for the other task value.

findings.summary: Every consumable name in _datasets.py (SCENARIOS, CPU_SCENARIOS, GPU_SCENARIOS, make_scenario_data, list_scenarios) is defined inside `if __name__ == "__main__":`, so on import (as bench_mrmr.py does) none of them exist, and the package's own documented entry point (`python -m ...bench_mrmr --scenarios all`) crashes with AttributeError.
findings.suggested_fix: Dedent the entire body (SCENARIOS through list_scenarios) out of the `if __name__` guard so it is bound at module import time.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST checker: for every `_*.py` module imported by a sibling module in the same package, verify every `module.attr` access resolves to a name bound at module scope in the imported file, not nested inside `if __name__ == "__main__":` or any other conditional.

findings.summary: np.asarray(df, dtype=float) returns a view (not a copy) into the DataFrame's backing buffer; the subsequent in-place a[np.isnan(a)]=0.0 silently mutates the shared df fixture, so all but the first timed call skip the NaN-scrub work, invalidating the benchmark's own reported speedup.
findings.suggested_fix: Force a copy before the in-place fix-up (np.array(df, dtype=float, copy=True) or .to_numpy(copy=True)), or rebuild df fresh inside the timed closure.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST/grep scanner: flag np.asarray(<pandas-obj>) / .values / .to_numpy() without copy=True immediately followed by an in-place index-assignment on the same local with no intervening .copy(); behaviourally, call the timed function twice and assert the source object's content hash is unchanged.

findings.summary: ck() writes to a hardcoded D:/Temp/synergy_scale_bench/progress.txt with no directory creation, so it crashes with FileNotFoundError on any host/session where that folder does not already exist, aborting long h1_bench.py/h2_bench.py sweeps immediately.
findings.suggested_fix: os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(PROG), exist_ok=True) at import time (or lazily in ck()), and make PROG overridable via an env var instead of a hardcoded D: path.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep-based scanner: flag any module-level string literal passed to open(..., "a"/"w") whose containing function has no reachable os.makedirs/Path.mkdir call.

findings.summary: TentativeRoughFix() computes its accept/reject medians over self.history_x including the phantom all-zero initializer row (row 0), biasing the tentative-feature decision; _io_plot.py's results_to_csv/plot explicitly strip this same row via .iloc[1:] but TentativeRoughFix does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Use hx.iloc[1:] (matching _io_plot.py's existing pattern) for both the per-tentative-feature median and the Max_Shadow median in TentativeRoughFix.
findings.meta_test_idea: Scanner: find attributes initialized via np.zeros(...) then grown by repeated np.vstack (the 'history_*' pattern); flag any consumer of the resulting DataFrame/array that does not slice off row 0 while a sibling consumer of the same attribute does.

findings.summary: The minority-class-vs-cv validation is gated on y_arr.dtype.kind in "iu" and silently skipped for float-dtype y (even integer-valued labels), so the intended clear early ValueError never fires and fit crashes deep inside sklearn instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Base the dtype gate on 'looks like a small integer-valued label alphabet' (mirroring _classify_target/_is_discrete_v2 used elsewhere in this package) instead of raw dtype.kind in 'iu'.
findings.meta_test_idea: Parametrized fuzz test: same minority-class-size violation across y dtypes {int64, float64, bool}; assert the identical clear ValueError fires for all three.

findings.summary: select_features_fdr is O(p^2) (nested Python loops scanning W.values() per candidate threshold) -- measured 6.4s at p=5000, contradicting _validate.py's own p>=5000 warning that recommends this exact function for 'sub-second selection on this scale'.
findings.suggested_fix: Sort abs_W once and use np.searchsorted/cumulative counts to compute n_neg/n_pos per threshold in O(p log p) total instead of the current O(p^2) double scan.
findings.meta_test_idea: Micro-benchmark CI gate asserting select_features_fdr on p=5000 synthetic W completes under ~0.5s.

findings.summary: integral_calibration_error_from_metrics accepts calibration_coverage (always passed by every caller) but never uses it in the formula — confirmed live that varying it 0.0/0.1/0.9 gives identical ICE; traced via git log -S to the function's original 2024 form, so this predates all module splits.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire calibration_coverage into the formula with an explicit coverage_weight knob, or remove the parameter and document that ICE ignores bin coverage.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST scanner flagging any function parameter that never appears as a Name/Load node in the function body — catches dead parameters in public metric APIs.

findings.summary: MBHOptimizer.submit_evaluations force-casts known_candidates to int, corrupting/mis-tracking a continuous (non-integer) search_space and causing re-suggestion of already-evaluated points.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve search_space's/known_candidates' natural dtype instead of hardcoding .astype(int).
findings.meta_test_idea: Run a full suggest/submit cycle with a float search_space (np.linspace) and assert every submitted candidate is excluded from later suggestions and dtype is preserved.

findings.summary: apply_quality_gate_kn slices level_models_and_predictions to gate survivors but returns the tag lists unsliced, breaking positional alignment used by compute_high_correlation_pairs / apply_diversity_drop downstream.
findings.suggested_fix: Slice _ensemble_member_tags/_ensemble_short_tags by _kept_idx exactly like sibling helpers catastrophic_drop_kn/catastrophic_drop_k2 already do.
findings.meta_test_idea: Fuzz test asserting len(members)==len(tags) for every returned tuple across the score.py gate pipeline, with a synthetic member forced to fail the K>2 quality gate.

findings.summary: CatboostParamsOptimizer's rule DSL references grow_policy/model_shrink_mode as required companion fields but never adds them to self.params, permanently vetoing boosting_type=='Ordered' and posterior_sampling=True from the HPT search space.
findings.suggested_fix: Add grow_policy and model_shrink_mode as real swept dimensions in self.params, or treat a missing key as 'equals CatBoost default' for these specific rules.
findings.meta_test_idea: Sample N=2000 candidates via generate_valid_candidates on a real CatboostParamsOptimizer and assert boosting_type=='Ordered' and posterior_sampling=True each survive check_rules at a nonzero rate.

findings.summary: additive_interaction_diagnostic's _cv_score indexes y[train_idx]/y[test_idx] directly; for a pandas Series y with a non-default index (the common real-world case), this performs label-based indexing instead of positional, silently misaligning train/test rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Coerce y = np.asarray(y) once at the top of the function, mirroring how X is already handled positionally via .iloc.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call the function with y as a pandas.Series built from a shuffled/non-contiguous index and assert results match the plain-ndarray call bit-for-bit.

findings.summary: interpolate=True fills a missing sibling group by interpolating over the POSITIONAL rank of groups, not the actual order_col value distance the docstring promises; reproduced with groups at order=(0,1,100) and values=(10,NaN,50) -- the missing middle group (order=1, near order=0) is filled with 30.0 (positional midpoint) instead of a value near 10.
findings.suggested_fix: Interpolate against the actual order_col values per group (set the interpolation index to group_order values, not a default RangeIndex) before falling back to ffill/global mean.
findings.meta_test_idea: Regression test with 3 unevenly-spaced groups asserting the interpolated fill is closer to the near neighbor (by order_col value) than the positional midpoint.

findings.summary: smoothed_target_encode_column computes train_encoded via y_train.groupby(train_series) over the same rows it then maps back onto -- every row's own target informs its own category's shrunk mean (in-sample, non-OOF target encoding), with no leakage-warning docstring unlike every other stateful-statistic function in this package.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a K-fold/leave-one-out OOF variant for train_encoded, or at minimum document the in-sample leakage risk as prominently as sibling modules (cleaning.py, outlier_capping_or_missing.py, rare_count_pruning.py) already do.
findings.meta_test_idea: Test asserting train_encoded's correlation with y_train on a purely-random (label-independent) categorical column stays near the smoothing-implied floor, not inflated by self-leakage; grep scanner for <series>.groupby(<same-frame-column>) mapped straight back onto that same frame without a fold split.

findings.summary: apply_gaussian_power_transform's Box-Cox replay path has no positivity guard (unlike the fit phase's explicit np.any(x<=0) check); reproduced: applying a fitted Box-Cox transform to inference data containing 0.0/-1.0 returns those values UNCHANGED (raw, untransformed), silently mixed into an otherwise properly-transformed column with no error or NaN signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the apply-phase branch the same way the fit phase does -- raise, return None, or clip/impute non-positive apply-time values before calling boxcox_apply, and document the choice.
findings.meta_test_idea: Regression test asserting apply_gaussian_power_transform raises or clearly flags (not silently passes through raw values) when apply-time data violates the Box-Cox positivity precondition the fit-time data satisfied.

findings.summary: _first_group_column's categorical-dtype detector is broken: `dt is object` never matches a real pandas object-dtype column (identity vs equality), and there is no polars dtype branch at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Use pd.api.types.is_object_dtype(col) / dt == object instead of `is`; add a polars branch (Categorical/Enum/Utf8/String via col.dtype, cardinality via col.n_unique()).
findings.meta_test_idea: AST/grep scanner flagging `\bis\s+(object|str|int|float|bool|dict|list|tuple)\b` outside isinstance(...) calls.

findings.summary: _ranked_top_features picks NaN-importance features as top-ranked because np.argsort(...)[::-1] sorts NaNs last ascending, first after reversal (empirically confirmed).
findings.suggested_fix: order = np.argsort(np.nan_to_num(imp, nan=-np.inf))[::-1], or filter NaNs before ranking.
findings.meta_test_idea: Property test with random importance vectors containing injected NaNs; assert returned top-k never includes a NaN-importance feature when enough non-NaN features exist. Same unguarded pattern recurs 3x more in sibling diagnostics_dispatch.py (out of scope, not fixed here).

findings.summary: Combined-HTML-report image resolver only tries .png and .matplotlib.png, but renderers/save.py's naming policy produces .plotly.png for any multi-format/multi-backend plot_outputs (e.g. the package's own docstring example 'plotly[html,png] + matplotlib[pdf]'), so it silently embeds broken links while still recording success.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the real saved path via renderers/save.py's own naming policy (shared helper) instead of a hardcoded 2-name guess; or pass through the actual per-chart output paths recorded at save time.
findings.meta_test_idea: Render via a 2-format/2-backend plot_outputs DSL then call build_combined_html_report; assert every path in the produced HTML exists on disk. Existing tests only use single-backend 'matplotlib[png]', confirmed via grep of test_diagnostics_dispatch_followup.py.

findings.summary: render_risk_coverage_diagnostic, render_model_card_diagnostic, render_split_comparison_from_suite, and render_decile_table_diagnostic (the dispatch/wiring layer) have zero direct test coverage; existing tests with similar names only exercise the underlying charts.* composer functions.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a direct test per wrapper (happy path + a None/empty/shape-mismatch edge case) asserting on metrics_dict['charts'] and any recorded scalar metrics, not just no-crash.
findings.meta_test_idea: Scanner: for every def render_*_diagnostic(/def render_*_from_suite( in reporting/, grep tests/ for a call to that exact function name; flag zero-hit functions.

findings.summary: weak_segment_heatmap digitizes a feature column that still contains NaN (by design, per its own docstring); numpy sorts NaN after every finite value, so np.digitize silently places every NaN row in the HIGHEST bin instead of excluding/flagging it, corrupting the worst-slice localization. Same missing-finite-filter pattern recurs in multiclass/multilabel _calib_grid_panel's digitize(proba_k, ...) calls.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly route NaN rows to a dedicated bin (as slice_finder._bin_matrix already does correctly) or exclude them from the digitize input and report their count separately; apply the same fix to the two _calib_grid_panel sites.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST/grep scanner: flag any np.digitize(X, edges) call where X's defining expression is not first passed through np.isfinite-based filtering in the same function. Pair with a property test injecting one NaN into a binning input and asserting it is excluded, not folded into the extreme bin.

findings.summary: _pick_base_column(train_df, y_train) receives the unfiltered full train_df while y_train is already sliced to train_idx, so every column length-check fails and the whole E3 distribution-driven-estimator injection feature silently never fires whenever there is a real train/val/test split.
findings.suggested_fix: In maybe_inject_distribution_driven_estimator, row-subset train_df by train_idx (flavour-native gather, no copy) before calling _pick_base_column, matching how y_train is already sliced.
findings.meta_test_idea: Fuzz the helper with a strict-subset train_idx plus a synthetic strongly-correlated column and assert it is actually selected; generic scanner for call sites passing a full frame alongside an index-sliced array to the same helper without also slicing the frame.

findings.summary: Row-subsetting falls back to np.asarray(X)[mask] when X lacks .loc (e.g. a polars DataFrame), silently flattening it to a raw/object-dtype ndarray and breaking fit/predict feature-name and dtype consistency; confirmed to emit a real sklearn feature-name mismatch warning and to produce mixed-type object arrays on any non-numeric polars column, unlike sibling modules (bagging.py, classification.py, glm.py) which handle polars explicitly.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the shared is_polars_df/row-gather pattern already used elsewhere in this package (e.g. bagging.py's _take_rows) instead of the bare hasattr(X,'loc') ternary.
findings.meta_test_idea: Parametrize composite estimator biz-value tests over pandas AND polars fixtures with a non-numeric column, asserting no crash and matching predictions; grep training/composite/** for hasattr(X,'iloc'/'loc') used as sole dispatch without a get_column/is_polars_df branch.

findings.summary: Same bug class as -2 in a sibling file: fit()/_predict_branch() row-subset via np.asarray(X)[mask] when X lacks .iloc, silently down-converting a polars DataFrame (which _concat_feature a few lines away DOES handle correctly, showing polars support was intended) to an untyped/object ndarray.
findings.suggested_fix: Same as -2: adopt the shared polars-aware row-gather helper instead of the ad hoc hasattr(X,'iloc') ternary.
findings.meta_test_idea: Same as -2's meta-test; also assert _concat_feature's polars branch is ever actually reachable given the upstream row-subset already downgraded the frame.

findings.summary: _leaf_weights_kernel / _LeafResidualForest._leaf_weights compute QRF membership weights via a full O(n_train) linear scan per (query, tree) pair instead of a leaf-bucketed lookup, giving O(n_query*n_trees*n_train) predict cost instead of O(n_query*n_trees*avg_leaf_size).
findings.suggested_fix: Precompute a CSR-style leaf->row-index bucket per tree at fit time (sort training rows by leaf id once) so predict-time work is proportional to the matching leaf size, not the full training set.
findings.meta_test_idea: Benchmark predict_quantile wall-time at fixed n_query/n_trees across n_train in {1k,10k,100k,1M} and assert near-linear (not quadratic) scaling; generalize as a scanner flagging predict-path kernels whose innermost loop bound is the training-set length rather than a leaf/bucket size.

findings.summary: _fit_final uses `except TypeError: model.fit(X, y)` to retry without sample_weight -- the exact anti-pattern post_shim.py (same directory) documents fixing; a TypeError from any other cause silently drops the confirmation-bias down-weighting of pseudo-labeled rows with no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse post_shim.py's has_fit_parameter-based signature gate (_model_fit_accepts_sample_weight) instead of catching TypeError, so only a genuine missing-parameter case skips sample_weight and any real fit error propagates.
findings.meta_test_idea: Mock estimator whose fit() accepts sample_weight but raises TypeError for an unrelated reason; assert _fit_final propagates rather than silently retrying unweighted. Repo-wide grep for `except TypeError:` guarding a `.fit(` retry without a signature check.

findings.summary: predict_quantile() never calls _soft_shrink.compute, so the default-ON out-of-range-base soft-shrink/smart-fallback protection that predict() applies is silently absent from every quantile/interval prediction.
findings.suggested_fix: In predict_quantile, after computing base_arr/domain_ok, call _soft_shrink.compute(self, transform, base_arr, params) (mirroring _predict_unclipped) and route _invert_one through the shrunk base_eff plus apply_smart_fallback for deep-OOD rows instead of the raw base_arr.
findings.meta_test_idea: For every ADDITIVE_BASE_TRANSFORMS member, predict() and predict_quantile(alpha=0.5) on the same out-of-fit-range rows and assert both stay inside the soft-shrink-bounded envelope; generically, flag any predict_quantile-shaped sibling of a predict function that skips a guard the sibling calls.

findings.summary: Near-duplicate-feature auto-drop's greedy chain-collapse can drop every column in a 3+ way mutually-correlated cluster (a triangle in the correlation graph), leaving zero survivors, instead of keeping exactly one.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 2-branch drop_set.add(...) heuristic with a union-find / connected-component pass: union both ends of every above-threshold pair, then keep exactly one representative per connected component and drop the rest.
findings.meta_test_idea: Property test: build a random correlation-pair graph (nodes=columns, edges=pairs above threshold, including a 3+-clique case), run the drop-selection function, assert every connected component retains >=1 undropped node. Generalizable to any 'drop one side of each correlated pair' helper in the codebase.

findings.summary: The identity-equivalent-pre_pipeline dedup 'break' exits the weight loop before _build_and_record_model_schema / pipeline_cache.set run, so the model that just trained gets no metadata['model_schemas'] entry, silently disabling predict-time schema-drift hard-fail protection for it.
findings.suggested_fix: Move _build_and_record_model_schema (+ _forward_dataset_reuse_cache, pipeline_cache.set) to before the identity-equivalent break check so the model that actually trained is always recorded.
findings.meta_test_idea: Integration test asserting metadata['model_schemas'] contains an entry for the first (model, weight) combo when skip_identity_equivalent_pre_pipelines fires; generalized as an early-exit-completeness AST/property scanner (break/return must not skip bookkeeping the normal path performs).

findings.summary: _validate_target_values silently swallows its own empty-classification-target diagnostic: the raise ValueError(...) message-format expression indexes arr_np.flat[0] on a 0-length array, raising IndexError before ValueError is constructed; the except ValueError: raise / except Exception: log.debug pair catches the IndexError in the generic branch and returns normally instead of raising anything.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard arr_np.size == 0 (or otherwise avoid indexing into a possibly-empty array) before formatting the ValueError message; narrow the surrounding except Exception so an error inside error-construction can't be silently absorbed.
findings.meta_test_idea: Scanner: flag any raise ValueError(f"...{arr[i]!r}...") (array indexing inside an f-string passed to raise) sitting inside a try whose except clause does not also explicitly catch IndexError/KeyError -- the message-construction code can itself fail and get silently reclassified as 'no error' by a broad sibling except Exception.

findings.summary: Bare `except Exception:` around the njit multilabel-stratification kernel call has zero logging and silently falls back to the ~50x slower pure-Python iterstrat path on any failure, including a genuine bug in the njit kernel.
findings.suggested_fix: Log a logger.warning naming the exception type/message before falling back, mirroring the fix already shipped for _select_mi_backend / plugin_mi_classif_batch_dispatch elsewhere in this codebase.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep/AST scanner: flag any except Exception block wrapping a call into a *_njit*/*_numba* module that contains no logger.* call in its body.

findings.summary: _get_training_configs_cached keys its process-lifetime cache partly on id(indexed_subgroups), a freshly-built short-lived dict; CPython id-reuse after GC of the previous target's dict can produce a stale cache hit mixing one target's fairness-subgroup-derived calibration metric config into another target's result.
findings.suggested_fix: Key on a cheap content fingerprint of indexed_subgroups (sorted group names + shapes/dtypes or a hash) instead of id(), or keep a strong reference alive alongside the cache entry to prevent id reuse.
findings.meta_test_idea: Force id-collision by del + gc.collect() between building two structurally-different indexed_subgroups dicts and assert the cache does not return the first result for the second.

findings.summary: _compute_oof_preds constructs GroupKFold(n_splits=1) outside its try/except when a train fold has only 1 distinct group, raising an uncaught ValueError that crashes the whole per-model training call after the model already trained.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the GroupKFold construction (and the group-cardinality computation) in the same try/except that guards cross_val_predict, or early-return (None, None) when n_unique_groups < 2.
findings.meta_test_idea: Fuzz group_ids down to 1 distinct group for every cross_val_predict-based OOF helper and assert a documented sentinel return instead of a raised exception.

findings.summary: _build_elasticnet_classifier silently ignores the user's configured l1_ratio and always uses the hardcoded fallback 0.15, because _get_l1_ratio gates on config.penalty=='elasticnet' which is never true (penalty defaults to 'l2' and nothing derives it from model_type='elasticnet').
findings.suggested_fix: Pass l1_ratio=config.l1_ratio directly in _build_elasticnet_classifier, or auto-derive penalty='elasticnet' from model_type in a LinearModelConfig validator.
findings.meta_test_idea: Build create_linear_model('elasticnet', LinearModelConfig(l1_ratio=0.9), use_regression=False) and assert get_params()['l1_ratio'] == 0.9.

findings.summary: On a train-Dataset cache hit, lgb_shim's fit() re-applies set_label/set_weight but never set_init_score, so a subsequent .fit(X, y, init_score=new_value) call reusing the cached Dataset silently trains against the stale/absent init_score instead of the new one.
findings.suggested_fix: Call dtrain.set_init_score(...) on cache hit (clearing to a zero-equivalent when init_score is omitted), mirroring the existing weight-reset-to-ones pattern.
findings.meta_test_idea: Fit the shim twice with the same X but two different init_score vectors and assert the second booster matches a from-scratch fit on the second init_score.

findings.summary: On a val-Dataset cache hit, lgb_shim only calls dval.set_weight() when w_val is not None; when a later call omits the eval-set weight after an earlier call supplied one, the reused Dataset keeps the stale weight instead of resetting to uniform -- asymmetric with the train-Dataset path in the same file and with xgb_shim.py's equivalent val-DMatrix handling.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an else branch calling dval.set_weight(np.ones(dval.num_data(), dtype=np.float32)) to mirror both the train-Dataset path and xgb_shim.py's val-DMatrix cache-hit handling.
findings.meta_test_idea: Fit with eval_sample_weight=[w], then refit the same instance with the same eval X and eval_sample_weight=None; assert the reused Dataset's weights are all-ones, not the stale w.

findings.summary: _calibration_block falls back to model_entry.test_target when oof_target is absent but oof_probs is present, then positionally truncates and zips oof_arr[:n] against test-split y_arr[:n] -- pairing train-row-ordered OOF probabilities with unrelated test-split labels, the exact leakage/misalignment bug class evaluation.py's post_calibrate_model explicitly guards against elsewhere in the same codebase.
findings.suggested_fix: Require oof_target alongside oof_probs (mirror post_calibrate_model's explicit ValueError when oof_probs is present but oof_target is missing) instead of silently falling back to test_target.
findings.meta_test_idea: Stamp oof_probs on a model entry with oof_target=None and a differently-valued test_target; assert _calibration_block returns status=skipped rather than a fabricated ok verdict.

findings.summary: MuonAdamWHybrid.param_groups is a disconnected placeholder list, not delegated to the wrapped Muon/AdamW optimizers, so any torch LR scheduler attached via configure_optimizers silently has zero effect on the real learning rates.
findings.suggested_fix: Give MuonAdamWHybrid the same param_groups delegation pattern SAM/Lookahead already use via _optimizer_wrapper_shared.wrapper_param_groups, fanning across both inner optimizers.
findings.meta_test_idea: Attach an LR scheduler to MuonAdamWHybrid, step it, assert the inner _muon/_adamw optimizers' actual lr changed; generalize as a rule that any Optimizer wrapping >1 inner optimizer must expose param_groups as a live property.

findings.summary: shapley_blend's degenerate-fallback branch silently returns an all-zero ensemble_pred (and all-zero weights) while still reporting a 'selected' model, when every model's raw Shapley value is <= 0.
findings.suggested_fix: In the fallback branch, set survivor_weights[best_idx] = 1.0 directly instead of relying on weights * keep_mask (which is 0 when the clipped weight of the argmax model is 0).
findings.meta_test_idea: Property test forcing every Shapley value <= 0 (mock score_fn to a constant) and assert ensemble_pred is not all-zero. Generalize: any function with a documented 'falls back to X' branch must be tested to actually return X's own values, not a zero/clipped-derived substitute.

findings.summary: 3 of 8 example imports in the root package's 'public API convention' docstring are broken ImportErrors against the current tree (MRMR, expected_calibration_error, predict_from_models).
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the three lines to real working paths (mlframe.feature_selection.filters.MRMR; the real ECE symbol in mlframe.metrics.calibration; mlframe.training.core.predict_from_models or re-export under mlframe.inference.predict); add a regression test.
findings.meta_test_idea: Regex-extract every 'from mlframe... import ...' line from package docstrings repo-wide and exec() each, failing on ImportError.

findings.summary: 10 of 35 sibling training/composite/*.py BaseEstimator regressors (direct_multi_horizon, dual_direction, orthogonal, per_group_router, regime_split_ensemble, segmented_model_factory, feature_subset_bagging, gated_regression_mixture, meta, simplex) lack sample_weight in fit() while 11+ siblings in the same package accept it, causing a hard TypeError for any caller threading sample_weight uniformly across the family.
findings.suggested_fix: Add sample_weight to the 10 listed fit() signatures where mathematically applicable, or raise a clear NotImplementedError with an explanatory docstring note where it genuinely isn't.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST scanner grouping BaseEstimator classes by directory/family, flagging fit() signatures missing sample_weight when >50% of siblings have it and no docstring opt-out marker exists.

findings.summary: 6 workflow files (ci.yml x2, mypy-full.yml, gpu-matrix.yml, gpu-extras-install-matrix.yml, sklearn-matrix-ci.yml, numba-coverage.yml) install sibling dep pyutilz via unpinned `git clone --depth 1` (default branch HEAD, no SHA) instead of a pinned commit, reproducing a documented prior incident class (X_SECURITY_API_PACKAGING-5) where an unpinned pyutilz commit silently broke MRMR.fit() for every caller.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin every direct clone to an explicit commit SHA (checkout after clone, or a PEP 508 git+...@sha install), bump deliberately with a CHANGELOG entry.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep every .github/workflows/*.yml for `git clone`/`pip install .*@ git+` targeting a first-party sibling repo and assert each is followed by a 40-char commit SHA checkout, not a bare branch clone.

findings.summary: pyproject.toml's dev extra pins ruff==0.16.0 with a comment claiming it matches .pre-commit-config.yaml's ruff-pre-commit rev, but all three ruff-pre-commit hooks there are pinned to v0.15.22 -- the exact stale-pin drift class the prior audit's F1 finding already fixed once, now recurred.
findings.suggested_fix: Bump .pre-commit-config.yaml's three rev: v0.15.22 entries to v0.16.0 (or drop pyproject.toml's pin back to 0.15.22) so the comment's claim is true again.
findings.meta_test_idea: Meta-test parsing the pinned ruff==X.Y.Z in pyproject.toml's dev extra and every rev: under ruff-pre-commit in .pre-commit-config.yaml, asserting equality.

findings.summary: The auto-merge eligibility regex requires a single 'from X.Y.Z to A.B.C' pair in the PR title, but dependabot.yml groups both ecosystems' routine bumps into one PR (grouped titles contain no such pair), so auto-merge silently never fires for the majority of PRs it exists to handle.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse Dependabot's grouped-PR body (which lists each dependency's from/to pair) instead of the title, or scope this workflow explicitly to ungrouped/security PRs and document the gap for grouped ones.
findings.meta_test_idea: Feed a real Dependabot grouped-PR title sample through the extracted bash regex and assert it correctly classifies as eligible or explicitly-deferred, not silently skipped.

findings.summary: The mypy-full-manual hook still uses --cache-dir=../.mlframe_mypy_cache_shared (cross-worktree shared cache), the exact pattern two sibling mypy hooks in the same file were moved off on 2026-08-03 after proving it can make a known-buggy revision silently report 'Success'.
findings.suggested_fix: Give mypy-full-manual its own local --cache-dir like its siblings, or remove it as redundant with the whole-project mypy-full hook.
findings.meta_test_idea: Meta-test parsing every mypy hook's --cache-dir in .pre-commit-config.yaml and asserting none resolve outside the current checkout (no ../ prefix).

findings.summary: [tool.ruff] extend depends on $PY_CI_SHARED_DIR, which is never set anywhere in the repo (no workflow, no .pre-commit-config.yaml, no CONTRIBUTING.md mention) -- a fresh contributor following the documented setup breaks on the very first pre-commit ruff hook.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the required py-ci-shared clone + env var export in CONTRIBUTING.md's setup section, or have the local hooks bootstrap it themselves.
findings.meta_test_idea: Run `pre-commit run --all-files` in a clean env with only the documented CONTRIBUTING.md steps applied and PY_CI_SHARED_DIR unset; assert it does not fail with a config-resolution error.

findings.summary: _calibration_block falls back from oof_target to test_target and positionally pairs oof_probs (train-row order) with test_target (a disjoint row set), producing a silently meaningless calibration/ECE diagnostic reported as status=ok.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the test_target fallback; return status=skipped when oof_target is absent, mirroring training/evaluation.py::post_calibrate_model's hard ValueError for the identical situation.
findings.meta_test_idea: Scanner: flag any getattr(x, 'oof_*', None) fallback to a differently-named *_target/*_probs attribute without an explicit row-count/index-identity check between the two sources.

findings.summary: test_many_nan_values's sole assertion sits inside a try/except Exception: pass, so AssertionError itself is swallowed -- the test cannot fail regardless of code correctness.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the assertion outside the try, or narrow the except to the specific expected failure modes, or split into a success-path test and an explicit pytest.raises failure-mode test.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST scanner flagging any try block with a top-level assert whose matching except handler catches Exception/BaseException (or bare except) without re-raising -- the assertion's failure path is provably unreachable.

findings.summary: test_best_weights_restoration / test_load_best_weights_in_ddp explicitly enable load_best_weights_on_train_end but their whole assertion body is 'if hasattr(model,"best_epoch"): assert best_epoch is not None' -- zero assertions execute if the attribute is absent, and even when present nothing verifies weights were actually restored.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare model state/weights (or held-out loss) at the best epoch against the state after restoration; drop the hasattr guard and fail loudly if the attribute is genuinely missing given the explicit config flag.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST scanner flagging test_* functions whose only assertion(s) are nested inside an `if hasattr(x, ...):` block with no else -- same vacuous-guard shape as the already-fixed stopfile-callback F7 finding from the 2026-07-21 cycle, recurring in a new subsystem.

findings.summary: apply_sticky_state_persistence_floor never validates that a per-class floor vector's length equals k (number of classes); a mismatched length causes an opaque IndexError from floor_arr[active] instead of a clear ValueError, unlike every other shape check in this function.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit ValueError check that floor_arr.shape[0] == k when floor_arr.ndim == 1.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call with floor=np.ones(k-1) and floor=np.ones(k+1) and assert a clear ValueError, not IndexError.

findings.summary: _emit_reliability_plot's build_reliability_overlay_spec call is not wrapped in try/except (only render_and_save is), and pick_best_calibrator calls _emit_reliability_plot with no enclosing handler, so a spec-build failure crashes the whole calibrator-selection call even though selection already succeeded and plotting is documented as an opt-in, failure-tolerant diagnostic.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the try/except in _emit_reliability_plot to also cover build_reliability_overlay_spec, returning None with a logged warning on failure.
findings.meta_test_idea: Monkeypatch build_reliability_overlay_spec to raise, call pick_best_calibrator(..., emit_plot=True), assert it still returns a normal result with plot_path=None.

findings.summary: _build_resample_indices's non-stratified branch fills the (n_bootstrap, n) index matrix via a Python loop calling rng.integers once per row instead of a single vectorized rng.integers(0, n, size=(n_bootstrap, n)) call, unlike the stratified branch which has an explicit justification for its own loop.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the per-row loop with one vectorized rng.integers call after verifying bit-identical draw order.
findings.meta_test_idea: Bit-identity test comparing the vectorized draw against the current per-row loop across several (n, n_bootstrap, seed) combinations, plus a wall-time bench at n_bootstrap=1000.

findings.summary: constant_group_target_scan(df, y, candidate_cols=[]) raises KeyError: 'min_group_variance_ratio' (confirmed) instead of returning an empty, correctly-columned DataFrame, because pd.DataFrame([]) has no columns for .sort_values(...) to find.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard: if not rows: return pd.DataFrame(columns=[...documented columns...]) before the sort_values call.
findings.meta_test_idea: Parametrized test calling every public rank_*/*_scan function in evaluation/ with its list-typed input set to [] and asserting a clean empty-DataFrame return, never a KeyError.

findings.summary: subpopulation_ratio_drift_check raises KeyError: 'prevalence_ratio' (confirmed) when train_df/test_df have zero effective values for subgroup_col (e.g. both empty), same pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(...)-without-empty-guard pattern as COMPETITION_EVALUATION-5.
findings.suggested_fix: Return an explicitly-columned empty DataFrame when all_values is empty, before the sort_values call.
findings.meta_test_idea: Same meta-test as COMPETITION_EVALUATION-5, applied to subpopulation_ratio_drift_check with zero-row train_df/test_df.

findings.summary: rank_subpopulation_drift_severity(train_df, test_df, subgroup_cols=[]) raises KeyError: 'drift_severity_score' (confirmed) instead of returning an empty ranking.
findings.suggested_fix: Same fix pattern as COMPETITION_EVALUATION-5/6.
findings.meta_test_idea: Same meta-test as COMPETITION_EVALUATION-5, applied to rank_subpopulation_drift_severity with subgroup_cols=[].

findings.summary: rank_subgroup_feature_overfit_risk(train_df, test_df, candidates=[]) raises KeyError: 'risk_score' (confirmed) instead of returning an empty ranking -- 4th independent occurrence of this same bug class in this cluster.
findings.suggested_fix: Same fix pattern as COMPETITION_EVALUATION-5/6/7.
findings.meta_test_idea: Given 4 independent occurrences, add a code_audit scanner rule flagging pd.DataFrame(rows) immediately followed by .sort_values(...) without an intervening 'if not rows:' guard.

findings.summary: bootstrap_auc_brier_ll_ece_batch drops non-finite per-resample values with no failure-count logging, unlike its documented 'bit-identical' sibling bootstrap_metrics which warns once failures exceed 25%; AUC can legitimately go NaN on unstratified resamples of imbalanced binary targets, so this fast path (now the default route per project history) silently loses the failure-rate diagnostic exactly where class imbalance matters most.
findings.suggested_fix: Track a per-metric failure count in the two _bootstrap_batch_* kernels (or count ~np.isfinite(raw) in the wrapper) and call the same log_throttle warning path bootstrap_metrics uses when failures exceed n_bootstrap // 4.
findings.meta_test_idea: Differential test comparing bootstrap_auc_brier_ll_ece_batch and bootstrap_metrics on a rare-positive, small-n, unstratified fixture chosen to produce a high single-class-resample rate; assert both emit a comparable failure-rate warning.

findings.summary: _sma_from_cumsum slices cumsum[:-window]; window=0 hits Python's arr[:-0]==arr[:0] trap, causing a shape-mismatch crash instead of a clear validation error.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate window >= 1 at the top of hull_moving_average / hull_moving_average_multi and raise ValueError.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST/grep scanner flagging arr[:-x] slices where x is a parameter with no proven-positive guard earlier in the function.

findings.summary: native_gpu_shap_available only catches AttributeError around get_booster(), but XGBoost raises NotFittedError for an unfitted model, so the documented 'never raises, returns False' contract is broken.
findings.suggested_fix: Also catch sklearn.exceptions.NotFittedError (or a broad Exception scoped to the fit-check) around the get_booster() call.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call every *_available()/*_supported() capability-probe function in the codebase with a deliberately-unfitted estimator and assert it returns bool rather than raising.

findings.summary: knn_shapley's k parameter is never validated; k<=0 divides by k inside the fastmath njit recursion, silently producing inf/nan Shapley values instead of raising.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'if k < 1: raise ValueError(...)' in knn_shapley before dispatching to _score_one_batch.
findings.meta_test_idea: Fuzz every public function taking an integer k/window/neighbours parameter with {-1, 0} and assert a clear ValueError, never silent NaN/Inf output.

findings.summary: visualize_prediction_vs_truth calls plt.subplots(1, len(samples)); when len(samples)==1 matplotlib returns a bare Axes (not an array), so axs[i] indexing raises TypeError.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass squeeze=False to plt.subplots and index axs[0, i], or wrap a scalar axs result in a list.
findings.meta_test_idea: Regression test calling visualize_prediction_vs_truth with a length-1 samples tuple and asserting no exception.

findings.summary: gmm_shift_diagnostics' shift_zscore is one-directional (only flags new_avg_loglik < train's), silently missing distribution shift toward HIGHER likelihood (e.g. new data collapsing near one component)
findings.suggested_fix: Use abs(shift_zscore) or a proper two-sample z/t test combining both train_std and new_scores.std()
findings.meta_test_idea: Construct a synthetic new_df with higher average log-likelihood than train and assert the diagnostic can still fire for a large shift

findings.summary: Module-level kernel_tuner registration loop has no try/except despite an adjacent comment claiming it is 'wrapped so a missing pyutilz / circular import never breaks the dispatcher' - the actual safety net lives only in the caller (_recursion_dispatch.py)
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the module-level registration loop in its own try/except, or correct the comment to describe where the real protection lives
findings.meta_test_idea: Simulate ImportError/AttributeError on pyutilz.performance.kernel_tuning.registry.kernel_tuner and assert `import mlframe.feature_engineering._recursion_autotune` does not raise

findings.summary: _frac_diff_single zero-fills any NaN in the input before convolving, so a NaN past the first K rows silently corrupts every downstream window that touches it (substituting 0, not propagating NaN); the public frac_diff docstring never documents this.
findings.suggested_fix: Propagate NaN through any window touching a NaN input (mask-weighted convolution, like local_linear_detrend already does), or explicitly document the zero-substitution risk in frac_diff's own docstring.
findings.meta_test_idea: Series with one NaN far past K; assert fractional-diff output for affected rows is NaN (once fixed) or is explicitly documented as zero-substituted.

findings.summary: compute_numaggs's len(arr)<=1 short-circuit always returns a raw Python NaN-tuple regardless of return_float32, while the normal path returns an np.float32 ndarray when return_float32=True -- a return-type inconsistency for degenerate short-input rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Route the degenerate case through the same return_float32 branch as the normal path.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call compute_numaggs(np.array([1.0]), return_float32=True) and assert the result is an np.float32 ndarray, matching normal-length input.

findings.summary: n_grid has no minimum-value validation; n_grid=1 triggers division by (n_grid-1)==0 inside the njit KDE grid construction, silently producing inf/NaN grid points instead of a clear error.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate n_grid >= 2 in both public functions, raising ValueError like sibling window_K checks elsewhere in the module family.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call with n_grid=1 and assert ValueError instead of silent NaN/garbage output.

findings.summary: Both flat and per-group NW smoothers scan the full reference set for every query (O(n_query*n_train)) even for the three compact-support kernels (epanechnikov/boxcar/tricube), which are provably zero outside the bandwidth -- no windowed/two-pointer fast path exploits this.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sorted-input windowed/binary-search fast path for the three compact kernels; keep the full scan only for gaussian.
findings.meta_test_idea: Perf bench: compact-kernel NW at large n with a narrow bandwidth should show a measured speedup once windowed.

findings.summary: _adasyn_synthesize's NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=k_global+1).fit(X_full) is never capped to X_full.shape[0], unlike every other kNN call in this package; crashes with ValueError on small folds/subsets.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap k_global to min(k_global, X_full.shape[0]-1) before constructing NearestNeighbors.
findings.meta_test_idea: Fuzz every compute_*_features function with n_train sized just below its largest internal k/n_neighbors parameter and assert graceful degradation, not a raise.

findings.summary: Output column names are hardcoded to _width_a01/_width_a02 regardless of the actual configurable alphas parameter values; mislabels columns for non-default alphas and IndexErrors/silently drops columns when len(alphas) != 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate len(alphas)==2 explicitly (matching distributional_moments.py's len(quantiles)!=7 guard) or derive column names dynamically from the actual alpha values.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call every compute_*_features function accepting a tuple-shaped parameter with a non-default-length tuple and assert output column count/names track the actual parameter, not the default.

findings.summary: Module docstring claims 'OOF LGB' reconstruction but _process fits and scores in-sample (same rows), understating the MAD residual scale and inflating downstream z-residual outlierness features; sibling files in the same cluster implement the OOF fix for the identical reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same inner-KFold(3) OOF pattern decision_region_depth.py uses for its oof_resid computation, or correct the docstring if OOF was aspirational.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep module docstrings for 'OOF' and cross-check the described code path actually contains a KFold/cross_val_predict call.

findings.summary: kNN graph construction queries a NearestNeighbors index fit on Xt_s with Xt_s itself using n_neighbors=k_graph (not k_graph+1), so each row's self-match occupies one of its k_graph slots, silently weakening graph connectivity vs. the correct pattern used in sibling files (local_density_gradient.py, spectral_attention.py's _build_knn_graph).
findings.suggested_fix: Request n_neighbors=k_graph+1 and drop the self-match column before building the sparse graph, matching the sibling pattern already used elsewhere in this cluster.
findings.meta_test_idea: Scanner: grep every NearestNeighbors(...).fit(A) followed by .kneighbors(A) on the same array; each must explicitly handle/drop the self-match or document why not.

findings.summary: Pairwise bin-combo encoding hardcodes bin0*100+bin1 with no validation against max_bins_per_feat (a public, caller-settable parameter); >=100 bins per feature silently collides distinct (bin0,bin1) pairs into the same combo code, corrupting combo_count/n_unique_combos features.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the radix from the actual max bin count at runtime, or use np.ravel_multi_index / tuple-based uniqueness instead of a fixed base-100 multiply.
findings.meta_test_idea: Property test with max_bins_per_feat forced above 100 asserting no two distinct (bin0,bin1) pairs collide; scanner for manual col_a*<const>+col_b radix encodings not derived from actual column cardinality.

findings.summary: Five files each independently duplicate a near-identical _fit_3baselines* helper (LGB depth-3 + LGB depth-5 + LogisticRegression/Ridge with try/except fallback); the duplication has already produced observable drift -- inconsistent log levels (info vs debug) and materially different degenerate-fold fallback semantics (zero-gradient vs class-prior) for the identical LogisticRegression-failure condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a single shared _fit_3_diverse_baselines helper (new sibling module, following the existing _hard_row_shared.py precedent) with a uniform failure-fallback contract; migrate all 5 call sites (and first-half-cluster siblings).
findings.meta_test_idea: AST/token near-duplicate detector across _fit_*baseline* helpers flagging >85% body-similarity clusters of 3+; diff their except/fallback branches specifically for log-level and fallback-value drift.

findings.summary: _legacy_hermite draws length_a/length_b via unseeded global np.random.randint(3, 8) while every other RNG use in the same file (data gen, optuna TPESampler seed=42, optimise_hermite_pair seed=42) is fully seeded, so the printed 'legacy' baseline MI is non-deterministic across runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass a seeded np.random.default_rng(seed) (or random.Random(seed)) into _legacy_hermite instead of using the legacy global np.random.randint.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep/AST scanner: flag any np.random.{randint,rand,randn,choice,shuffle,permutation} call in a file that elsewhere also constructs a seeded np.random.default_rng(...) Generator -- mixing legacy global RNG with a seeded Generator in one reproducibility-sensitive script is the bug pattern.

findings.summary: row["auc_mean"] is gated on any(aucs.values()) instead of any(v is not None for v in aucs.values()); if one model produces a legitimate AUC of exactly 0.0 while the others failed (None), the truthy check misfires and the real result is silently dropped as None.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `any(aucs.values())` with `any(v is not None for v in aucs.values())`.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep for any()/all() applied directly to dict.values() in a function that elsewhere filters the same dict with `if v is not None`; flag as a truthy-vs-None mismatch.

findings.summary: Legacy ensure_batch_pair_mi_tuning/_run_sweep_batch_pair_mi (and 3 siblings in _auto_tune_sweeps_b.py) remain fully implemented and exported after migration to the new pyutilz kernel_tuner registry; cli.py's own docstring documents that this exact legacy sweep 'silently shadowed the new dispatcher' by writing to the same cache key without a code_version, yet the dangerous function is still reachable by anyone who imports it directly instead of going through the CLI.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the four superseded sweep bodies, or turn them into stubs that raise/redirect to the new registry, now that cli.py no longer calls them.
findings.meta_test_idea: For every kernel_name registered via the new kernel_tuner(...) registry, grep for any other function calling KernelTuningCache.update("<same name>", ...) directly; flag dual writers to one cache key.

findings.summary: h1_bench.py, h1_gpu_large.py, and h2_bench.py all sys.path.insert(0, r"D:/Upd/Programming/PythonCodeRepository/mlframe/src") — a dev-machine-specific absolute path that, if present but stale on some machine, silently shadows the properly installed mlframe package for the whole process.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the hardcoded sys.path insert; rely on the installed/editable package like every other _benchmarks script.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep scanner for sys.path.insert/append calls with an absolute drive-lettered or home-directory path literal.

findings.summary: find_sample() starts its KS-test sample search at element=1 (~10% of rows) instead of 0 (~5%), contradicting its own docstring, and raises IndexError on frames with <=2 rows under sample=True because get_5_percent_splits can return an array shorter than 2 elements.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the search at element=0; clamp/guard element against len(size) before the first size[element] access.
findings.meta_test_idea: Property test: for functions indexing a precomputed step/grid array from a nonzero literal start offset, fuzz tiny input sizes (n=0,1,2,3) and assert no IndexError and no deviation from the documented starting fraction.

findings.summary: estimate_features_relevancy divides by len(feature_columns) with no zero guard; a bins frame containing only target columns (no candidate features) raises ZeroDivisionError instead of returning an empty/graceful result.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard len(feature_columns) == 0 up front and short-circuit to an empty relevancy result before the ceil-adjustment division.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep-based scanner for '/ len(<expr>)' not preceded by a truthiness/length guard in the same function; fuzz each such function with an empty collection as the divisor source.

findings.summary: stability_selection dispatches to _fit_stability_selection BEFORE the estimators_list presence check a few lines later, so RFECV(stability_selection=True) with no estimator crashes with a confusing AttributeError from sklearn.base.clone(None) instead of RFECV's own clear ValueError.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the estimator-presence ValueError check above the stability_selection early-return, or duplicate the same guard at the top of _fit_stability_selection.
