findings.meta_test_idea: Call every top-level RFECV mode flag (stability_selection=True, multioutput_strategy=..., default) with estimator=None, estimators=None and assert the identical ValueError message fires in every mode.

findings.summary: RFECV.transform() unconditionally passes self_destruct=True to polars' to_pandas() for a polars X, unlike the sibling fit-path (_fit_init.py) which gates the identical kwarg combination behind an ownership marker specifically to avoid destroying a caller-owned frame's data. Direct testing on the installed polars 1.41.2 did not reproduce actual corruption, so this is a design-consistency / latent-risk gap rather than a confirmed data-loss bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same _frame_is_internally_owned/explicit-opt-in gate used in _init_fit_state to the polars branch of transform().
findings.meta_test_idea: Regression test: call .transform() twice on the SAME caller-owned polars DataFrame and assert byte-identical results both times, to catch a future polars version where self_destruct becomes destructive here.

findings.summary: _conditional_permutation_importance's single-feature (p==1, no-conditioning-set) fallback branch calls model.score() with no try/except, unlike the general (p>1) branch a few lines below which explicitly wraps the identical call so a scorer crash degrades to NaN instead of aborting the whole per-fold FI computation.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the p==1 branch's model.score(...) call in the same try/except-then-NaN pattern already used by the conditioning-set branch immediately below it.
findings.meta_test_idea: Pass a model whose .score() raises on the permuted single-column X and assert _conditional_permutation_importance returns a NaN entry instead of propagating the exception.

findings.summary: format_classification_report's MACRO-AVG CAVEAT docstring describes the deflating macro_over_present=False legacy behavior and claims it matches sklearn, but the function actually inherits fast_classification_report's default macro_over_present=True (present-classes-only, which is what really matches sklearn) — confirmed live with a 3-class example (0.875 actual vs 0.583 as the docstring implies).
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the caveat to describe the present-only default actually in effect.
findings.meta_test_idea: Unit test asserting macro avg does NOT deflate when a declared class is absent, pinning the documented (and actual) contract.

findings.summary: _spearmanr_scalar_njit's leading NaN pre-check loop has an early `return` inside `prange`, which Numba cannot parallelize (confirmed via NumbaPerformanceWarning reproduced in isolation); the docstring's '2-way prange... 1.5-2.7x' claim overstates achieved parallelism whenever the loop runs (i.e. every call).
findings.suggested_fix: Split the NaN check into a separate reduction-only loop (accumulate a bad-flag via +=, check after) matching the pattern already used correctly elsewhere in this codebase.
findings.meta_test_idea: CI check compiling every @njit(parallel=True) function under warnings-as-errors and asserting no NumbaPerformanceWarning fires on a representative call.

findings.summary: optimal_threshold (and optimal_ordinal_cutpoints in _ordinal_cutpoints.py:61-127) fit a parameter by maximizing a metric on the exact (y_true,y_score) supplied, with no HOLDOUT CONTRACT warning — inconsistent with this same package's own established pattern (quantile.py's coverage()/pit_values() carry explicit holdout-contract docstrings for a lower-risk read-only case).
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same HOLDOUT CONTRACT docstring paragraph used in quantile.py to both functions.
findings.meta_test_idea: Lint rule: any public optimal_*/fit_*/*_cutpoints/*_threshold function that both consumes y_true and returns a fitted value used to score new data must contain 'holdout' in its docstring.

findings.summary: tuning.py defines no __all__ (unlike sibling rf_proximity.py), so models/__init__.py's star-import leaks 13 third-party symbols (pd, np, db, uniform, loguniform, randint, KFold, train_test_split, cross_validate, check_scoring, Enum, auto) and the mutable global trained_models into mlframe.models's public API, verified empirically via mlframe.models.__all__.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit __all__ to tuning.py listing only the intended public surface.
findings.meta_test_idea: Extend the existing test_f5_package_has_curated_all meta-test to assert every name in each curated __all__ resolves to an object whose __module__ starts with 'mlframe'.

findings.summary: check_rules's allow_if_values_or branch re-uses the gate loop's leftover 'condition' variable; harmless (dead code) when conditions is non-empty but raises NameError when conditions is an empty tuple, an otherwise-legal DSL input.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the redundant re-check (the 'if not skip' guard already proves it), or explicitly handle empty conditions before the loop.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call check_rules(params, allow_if_values_or={(): [{'x': 1}]}) and assert it does not raise NameError.

findings.summary: favorize_unexplored's order parameter (docstring: 'combinations of order N') is never referenced in the function body; only single categorical values are ever favorized regardless of the order argument.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement true order-N combination tracking, or remove the parameter and correct the docstring.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST/grep unused-parameter scanner over public function signatures flagging parameters never referenced as a Name node in the body.

findings.summary: masked_multilabel_logloss_objective's care_mask uses exact float equality against a sentinel that has round-tripped through XGBoost's internal float32 label storage; a non-default sentinel not exactly representable in float32 would silently fail to mask 'don't care' cells.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the sentinel round-trips exactly through float32 (raise otherwise), or compare via explicit float32 casts on both sides.
findings.meta_test_idea: Build a DMatrix with a sentinel that does not round-trip exactly through float32, run the objective, and assert cells are still correctly masked or a clear error is raised.

findings.summary: combine_probs's 'qube' underflow guard is gated on a global (stacked > 0).all() over the whole tensor; a single exact-zero cell anywhere disables the underflow-protection clip for the entire tensor, including unrelated tiny-positive cells that need it.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the floor elementwise only where already positive: np.where(stacked > 0, np.clip(stacked, 1e-103, None), stacked).
findings.meta_test_idea: Build an array with one exact 0.0 cell and a separate 1e-150 cell; assert combine_probs(flavour='qube') doesn't lose precision on the tiny-positive cell.

findings.summary: enrich_ensemble_preds_with_numaggs mutates a caller-supplied numaggs_kwds dict in place via .update() instead of working on a local copy.
findings.suggested_fix: numaggs_kwds = dict(numaggs_kwds or {'whiten_means': False}) before any .update() calls.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call the function with an explicit kwargs dict, then assert the dict is unchanged after the call (compare to a pre-call snapshot).

findings.summary: clusterize's show_plot=True (default) path builds the full matplotlib figure, computes all scatter data, sets title/annotations, then immediately calls plt.close(fig) without ever calling .show(), saving, or returning it -- so the default call produces no visible or persisted output at all despite the docstring's 'render a scatter plot of the clusters' promise.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the Figure object so callers can display/save it themselves, or accept a save_path parameter; at minimum document that show_plot=True currently only computes-and-discards the figure.
findings.meta_test_idea: Test calling clusterize(show_plot=True) asserting a Figure object (or saved file) is actually produced/returned, not silently discarded.

findings.summary: apply_outlier_policy recomputes cap bounds from whatever X it is called on every time (no fit/apply split, no persisted state) and, unlike its sibling outlier_capping_or_missing.py, carries no leakage/fit-on-train-only caveat in its docstring; calling it independently on train and test silently diverges the cap bounds applied to each.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same explicit fit-on-train-only caveat outlier_capping_or_missing.py carries, or add a fit_outlier_policy_bounds/apply_outlier_policy_bounds split matching the fit_*/apply_* pattern used elsewhere in this package.
findings.meta_test_idea: Regression test asserting apply_outlier_policy(train,...) and apply_outlier_policy(test,...) called independently produce different cap bounds when train/test distributions differ.

findings.summary: Package-level __init__.py omits the fit_*/apply_* leakage-safe function pairs for rare_count_pruning, missing_indicator_pairing, and regime_conditioned_imputation (only the combined convenience wrapper is exported), even though each module's docstring recommends the split; confirmed 'from mlframe.preprocessing import fit_rare_category_collapse' raises ImportError while the analogous apply_feature_direction IS exported.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the missing fit_*/apply_* names to __init__.py's import list for parity with align_feature_direction.py/gaussian_power_transform_search.py.
findings.meta_test_idea: Test asserting every public fit_X/apply_X pair defined in a preprocessing/*.py module's own __all__ is also reachable from mlframe.preprocessing (package-level __all__ superset check).

findings.summary: _get_nunique's float fast path only extracts skip_vals[0]/skip_vals[1] into skip0/skip1; any 3rd+ element of a longer skip_vals tuple is silently dropped with no validation, diverging silently from the np.unique fallback path (which supports arbitrary-length skip_vals) if a future caller passes more than 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit 'if skip_vals and len(skip_vals) > 2: raise ValueError(...)' guard, or extend the njit kernel to accept a variable-length skip array.
findings.meta_test_idea: Unit test calling _get_nunique with a 3-element skip_vals on a float array asserting either correct behavior or a clear ValueError, not a silently wrong count.

findings.summary: render_category_discriminability_diagnostic accepts seed: int = 0 but never uses it; the composer it calls (compose_category_discriminability_figure) doesn't even accept a seed kwarg and hardcodes np.random.default_rng(0) internally for its row subsample. Every sibling render_* function in the same file correctly threads its seed through.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire seed through to the composer/panel builder (replacing the hardcoded default_rng(0)), or drop the dead parameter from the signature.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep every render_*_diagnostic/render_*_from_suite for a seed param, then grep its body for seed= passed to the composer call; flag accepted-but-unused seed params.

findings.summary: DIAG_ROW_CAP=100_000 / DIAG_MAX_FEATURES=200 are independently redefined here with the same names/values as diagnostics_dispatch.py:34,37 (the actual consumer), instead of importing from it; the copy here is dead except for re-export via __all__.
findings.suggested_fix: Import DIAG_ROW_CAP/DIAG_MAX_FEATURES from diagnostics_dispatch (or a shared constants module) instead of copy-pasting the literals.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep-based duplicate-constant scanner: flag any module-level NAME=<literal> whose exact (name, literal) pair also occurs in a sibling file within the same package with no import relationship between them.

findings.summary: When target_type authoritatively selects the multiclass or binary branch but the actual probs shape doesn't satisfy that branch's guard, the function silently falls through to return None with no log line; the multilabel branch a few lines above does log a warning on its analogous shape mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add logger.warning in the multiclass and binary branches mirroring the multilabel one when the shape guard fails but the target_type/panels gate matched.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call render_multi_target_panels with target_type='multiclass_classification' and a 2-column probs (below the >=3 classes guard); assert a warning is logged, not just that the return is None.

findings.summary: render_split_error_diagnostics passes timestamps=None to worst_k_table whenever the frame is subsampled (n > DIAG_ROW_CAP = 100k rows) instead of indexing timestamps by sample_idx like yt/yp are, silently dropping temporal context on exactly the large-frame (100GB+) case this subsystem targets.
findings.suggested_fix: Index timestamps[sample_idx] (bounded to the same DIAG_ROW_CAP subsample) instead of unconditionally passing None.
findings.meta_test_idea: Parametrized test calling render_split_error_diagnostics with n > DIAG_ROW_CAP and timestamps supplied; assert the returned worst_k_table has a non-null timestamp column. Generalize to every optional kwarg (ids, feature_importances) threaded through a subsample branch in this dispatcher.

findings.summary: MatplotlibRenderer._histogram's bar-width expression `float(p.bin_width or (bin_centers[1]-bin_centers[0]) if len(bin_centers)>1 else 1.0)` relies on Python ternary binding looser than `or`, parsing as `(p.bin_width or diff) if len>1 else 1.0` -- an explicitly-supplied bin_width is silently discarded and forced to 1.0 on a single-bin histogram. PlotlyRenderer._histogram (line 477) has the identical expression but correctly parenthesized, so the two backends render a single-bin histogram at different widths from the same spec.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the ternary in parens to match plotly.py: p.bin_width or ((bin_centers[1]-bin_centers[0]) if len(bin_centers)>1 else 1.0).
findings.meta_test_idea: Generic AST checker for `A or B if C else D` (no parens) anywhere in the repo. Plus a cross-backend parity test comparing both renderers' resolved bar width across bin_centers length in {0,1,2,N} x bin_width in {None, explicit}.

findings.summary: Three call sites still loop per-cell calling colors.auto_text_color() individually for heatmap cell-text color, even though colors.auto_text_colors_batch() exists specifically to replace this pattern (its own docstring documents the fix) and is already used by PlotlyRenderer._heatmap. Bounded by a 400-cell cap so not catastrophic, but a real missed optimization and 3-way code duplication.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace all three per-cell loops with one auto_text_colors_batch(...) call, mirroring renderers/plotly.py:569-574.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep scanner flagging any nested double for-loop under reporting/ whose body calls auto_text_color( -- require auto_text_colors_batch instead.

findings.summary: _top_split_features's sklearn-unavailable fallback ranks a feature via a median split (np.median, not np.nanmedian); a column with any NaN makes the median NaN, so both comparison masks (> med, <= med) are all-False, hi/lo come back empty, and that column's surrogate importance silently stays 0.0 regardless of its real discriminating power on non-missing rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Use np.nanmedian for the split point and mask NaN rows out of hi/lo (or pre-drop NaN per-column before the median).
findings.meta_test_idea: Property test: force the ImportError fallback path, feed a matrix where exactly one strongly-discriminating column has a single NaN, assert its surrogate importance is not zero.

findings.summary: factorize()'s no-pandas fallback (np.unique(..., return_inverse=True)) does not map NaN/null group labels to code -1 the way the pandas branch does, contradicting the function's own documented contract; downstream group reports would silently treat a NaN group as real data in the fallback-only path.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly NaN-mask and assign -1 in the np.unique fallback branch to mirror pd.factorize's contract.
findings.meta_test_idea: Parametrized test forcing the no-pandas branch (monkeypatch _HAVE_PANDAS=False) and asserting NaN labels map to -1 identically to the pandas path.

findings.summary: Per-candidate-column median imputation is computed once over the whole screening split BEFORE the StratifiedKFold loop (both stage-1 and stage-2), so each fold's train-side imputed values incorporate information from that fold's own held-out validation rows -- a train/val boundary leak of a summary statistic that mildly inflates margin_gain/cv_gain.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the imputation median from col[tr] only, inside each fold, and apply it to both col[tr] and col[va].
findings.meta_test_idea: Perturb only validation-fold values and assert the reported per-fold cv_gain is unaffected under a properly fold-local imputation; generic scanner for a summary statistic computed outside a CV split loop but later indexed by [tr]/[va] inside it.

findings.summary: predict_cdf builds a dense (n_rows, K, len(y_grid)) boolean broadcast array to derive the step-CDF, an unguarded O(n*K*G) memory allocation inconsistent with the rest of this package's careful bounded-memory reduction discipline; can allocate tens of GB at realistic large-n plus a moderately fine y_grid.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 3-D broadcast with a per-grid-point vectorized searchsorted scan (O(n*K) or O(n*log K)), or document/gate a size ceiling on n * len(y_grid).
findings.meta_test_idea: A memory-bound regression test (tracemalloc) on a large synthetic n * y_grid combination; generic scanner for triple-broadcast [..., None]/[None, ...] arrays whose 3 axes are all caller-controlled sizes with no documented bound.

findings.summary: CompositeOrRawStacker.fit computes n_splits = max(2, min(self.n_splits, n)); for n=0 or n=1 this still returns 2, so KFold(n_splits=2) raises sklearn's raw internal ValueError instead of a clear, class-named error.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate n>=2 up front and raise a clear ValueError naming the estimator and the row-count problem, or provide a documented degenerate fallback for tiny n.
findings.meta_test_idea: Fit CompositeOrRawStacker on n=0 and n=1 rows and assert a clear, actionable error rather than sklearn's internal KFold traceback; generalize as a fuzz sweep of every composite estimator at n in {0,1}.

findings.summary: _compute_offsets's docstring claims a 'vectorised groupby pass' but the implementation is a plain Python for-loop with .tolist()/dict accumulation -- materially slower than a vectorized groupby on the million-row panel data this estimator targets, and the docstring is misleading about the mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with pandas.Series(y).groupby(ids).agg(['sum','count']) or np.bincount on factorized ids for true vectorized O(n) aggregation, and correct the docstring.
findings.meta_test_idea: Bench _compute_offsets against a vectorized groupby baseline at n=1M rows and assert the gap stays within a small documented multiplier; doc-lint scanner flagging 'vectorised'/'one pass' docstring claims over a function body containing a bare for-loop over .tolist().

findings.summary: _ivap_saddle_njit is explicitly self-documented as O(g^2) in the number of unique calibration scores (outer max-over-lo rescan), with no size guard/cap/warning for a caller calibrating on a large, mostly-continuous-score calibration split.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a size guard/warning above a configurable g threshold, or implement the O(g log g) monotone-stack construction the docstring itself gestures at for the outer scan.
findings.meta_test_idea: Bench calibrate_venn_abers wall-time vs n_cal at {1k,5k,20k,50k} with continuous scores and assert sub-quadratic scaling, or a regression test pinning a documented g-threshold warning.

findings.summary: melt_to_long_gbm_features's within-column frequency count uses groupby(['_feature_name','_value']).transform('count') with pandas' default dropna=True, so any row whose original X value is NaN silently gets a NaN '_count' instead of a valid count -- no test/doc coverage for X containing missing values.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass dropna=False to the groupby call so NaN-valued rows form their own group, or explicitly document/handle the NaN-count case before X_long is built.
findings.meta_test_idea: Unit test calling melt_to_long_gbm_features with NaN-containing X and asserting no unexpected NaN in '_count' (or context columns); repo-wide scanner for .groupby([...]).transform( sites without an explicit dropna= where the grouper key can be NaN.

findings.summary: Bootstrap MI-gain CI raises an uncaught IndexError (crashing the whole fit() call) when mi_gain_bootstrap_n=1 and that lone replicate fails, because `boot_finite.size >= bootstrap_n // 2` is trivially true (0>=0) even for an empty array.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard with `boot_finite.size > 0 and boot_finite.size >= bootstrap_n // 2` before calling np.percentile(boot_finite, 2.5).
findings.meta_test_idea: Fuzz any `size_guard = n // k` pattern feeding np.percentile/np.median/np.quantile with n in {0,1,2} and an all-failing inner computation; flag guards that admit size==0.

findings.summary: Module-level _KEEP_MASK_CACHE (shared across all CompositeTargetDiscovery instances/threads in-process) is read via .get()+move_to_end() WITHOUT the lock that guards every write/evict path (popitem+__setitem__), risking a KeyError or corrupted LRU order under concurrent fit() calls.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend _KEEP_MASK_CACHE_LOCK to cover the read-and-touch (get + move_to_end) sequence, not just the write path.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep for module-level mutable caches where a Lock/RLock guards some access sites but not others in the same file; flag any unlocked .get()/[...] read on a cache with a sibling locked write.

findings.summary: A fully-implemented, unit-tested calibration-aware ranking-penalty module is never imported or called by any discovery gate (_tiny_rerank.py, _filter_and_gate.py, etc.) -- confirmed by repo-wide grep, zero production call sites.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire calibration_adjusted_score into _tiny_model_rerank's per-spec scoring (it already computes the OOF/in-fold residuals this module needs), or remove the module and its test with a documented rejection rationale per the REJECTED!=DELETED convention.
findings.meta_test_idea: Reachability scanner: for every non-__init__, non-test module in a package, flag it if every cross-reference to its public symbols resolves only to __init__.py re-exports and tests/.

findings.summary: linear_residual_multi_robust reuses the exact same forward/inverse functions as linear_residual_multi but is missing from ADDITIVE_BASE_TRANSFORMS, so it silently never gets the soft-base-shrink OOD guard its byte-identical sibling gets.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "linear_residual_multi_robust" to ADDITIVE_BASE_TRANSFORMS in _soft_shrink.py.
findings.meta_test_idea: For every pair of registry entries whose forward/inverse function objects are identity-equal, assert identical membership in every transform-name-keyed capability/guard set.

findings.summary: Developer-flagged (!TODO!) unresolved inefficiency: CB/LGB/XGB inner feature matrices (Pool/Dataset/DMatrix) are rebuilt once per target inside the per-target loop instead of once per shared feature-set, wasting binning/encoding work on multi-target suites.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache the built Pool/Dataset/DMatrix by (feature-set signature, model family) across the target loop and reuse via the existing label/weight-swap capability already probed in _detect_dataset_reuse_capabilities.
findings.meta_test_idea: Perf regression test: multi-target suite (K>=3 targets sharing feature columns) with cb/lgb; count-patch the Pool/Dataset constructor and assert call count is O(1) in K, not O(K).

findings.summary: _run_one_weight_iteration (451 LOC) is a full duplicate of the inline per-(model,weight) loop body in _phase_train_one_target_body.py but has zero call sites anywhere in src/ -- an abandoned monolith-split extraction that independently reproduces the TRAINING_CORE_B-1 bug and risks silent fix-divergence.
findings.suggested_fix: Either delete the unreachable file, or finish the extraction by making _phase_train_one_target_body.py actually call it and removing the inline duplicate -- do not leave both copies coexisting.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST-based orphan-symbol scanner over src/ flagging any module-level function/class with zero call sites outside its own definition file and no test import -- a strong signal of abandoned refactors.

findings.summary: ordered_target_encode_batch lacks the noise_count_halflife parameter its sibling ordered_target_encode exposes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add noise_count_halflife to the batch signature and apply the same per-column decay logic.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST scanner: for any f/f_batch sibling pair, flag when the batch variant's keyword-only param set is a strict subset of the singular variant's.

findings.summary: feature_handling_apply's target-encoder path never threads sample_weight into LeakageSafeEncoder, and no config field exposes one.
findings.suggested_fix: Add sample_weight to feature_handling_apply's signature and thread it into _apply_target_encoder's fit closure.
findings.meta_test_idea: Static call-graph scanner: flag any call site that doesn't forward an in-scope sample_weight variable to a callee whose signature declares one.

findings.summary: plot_target_over_time hardcodes ax.set_ylim(-0.02, 1.05) even for target_type='regression', where target_rate is an unbounded mean(y), breaking the chart.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive ylim from the actual target_rate range when target_type != binary_classification; scale drift_warn_threshold similarly.
findings.meta_test_idea: Parametrized test asserting ax.get_ylim() actually contains the data range for a regression TemporalAuditResult with large target_rate values.

findings.summary: is_neural_model() includes literal 'recurrent' in its alias set but MODEL_STRATEGIES has no 'recurrent' key; live-verified is_neural_model('recurrent')=True while get_strategy('recurrent') warns and mis-routes to TreeModelStrategy. Same bug class already fixed once in _helpers_training_configs.py.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop 'recurrent' from the alias tuple; deduplicate against training.models.is_neural_model (the version all real call sites actually use) so alias lists can't drift apart again.
findings.meta_test_idea: Cross-consistency test: for every is_X/get_X registry pair, assert every literal in is_X's alias set resolves via get_X without an unknown-model fallback.

findings.summary: _align_xgb_cat_categories's docstring claims the union of category levels spans 'all three splits' (train/val/test) so 'val/test' become a subset of the train universe, but the actual (correct, leak-safe) implementation deliberately unions only train+val, excluding test to avoid feeding test categories back before fit. The stale docstring could mislead a future edit into reintroducing the leak it currently prevents.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the docstring to describe the actual train+val-only union and the NaN-for-unseen-test-category semantics, matching the correct in-line comment already present in the loop body.
findings.meta_test_idea: Doc-consistency lint: grep docstrings claiming 'all three splits' / 'train/val/test union' semantics and cross-check the function body actually touches all three named split variables the way described.

findings.summary: save_mlframe_model's pre-pickle walk (_collect_pre_dump_swaps) mutates the SHARED nested object graph in place (torch.compile swap, Lightning-bloat nulling) and restores only in a finally block; lean=True only shallow-copies the top-level SimpleNamespace, so nested sub-objects are the same live references the caller's model still holds. Two concurrent save_mlframe_model calls on bundles sharing a nested sub-object (e.g. parallel per-model saves) can interleave the strip/restore windows.
findings.suggested_fix: Deep-copy (or clone at every mutated node) before stripping, or serialize under a per-object lock so concurrent saves of overlapping graphs can't interleave.
findings.meta_test_idea: Concurrency regression test: two SimpleNamespace bundles sharing one nested fitted-model object, saved from two threads simultaneously with an injected delay in the strip step; assert the shared object's attributes are correctly restored after both calls and both files deserialize with non-null attributes.

findings.summary: smearing_predict builds an unbounded (n_test, n_cal) dense broadcast array with no size gate on n_test, risking OOM on large predict batches (e.g. 32GB at n_test=2M, max_cal=2000).
findings.suggested_fix: Chunk over p in fixed-size row batches, accumulating incrementally so peak memory is O(chunk_size * max_cal) regardless of n_test.
findings.meta_test_idea: Test with n_test in the millions under a bounded peak-RSS assertion, or a static check flagging unchunked outer-product broadcasts in this module.

findings.summary: _get_neural_components caches only the import-success path; a broken (not merely absent) mlframe.training.neural install causes every subsequent call to retry the same documented 30-180s import chain.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a distinct sentinel for a cached failure (e.g. a module-level bool) so a genuine ImportError short-circuits future calls instead of retrying.
findings.meta_test_idea: Monkeypatch the neural import to raise on 1st and 2nd calls, call _get_neural_components twice, and assert the import was only attempted once.

findings.summary: _probe_available_memory_bytes's process-wide first-successful-probe cache doesn't distinguish a CPU-RAM probe from a GPU-VRAM probe; a call in one mode followed by a call expecting the other mode silently reuses the first probe's (very different magnitude) value, risking a CUDA OOM the module exists to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Key _PROBE_MEM_CACHE on (cuda_ok,) or device_id instead of a single scalar so CPU-mode and GPU-mode probes never collide.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call _probe_available_memory_bytes(cuda_available=False) then cuda_available=True with different monkeypatched probe values and assert the second call returns the GPU value, not the cached CPU value.

findings.summary: _compute_drift_invariant forwards feature_names to the numeric z-stat computation but not to compute_categorical_drift_psi, so a caller restricting compute_feature_distribution_drift to a feature subset gets that restriction honored only on the numeric side, not the categorical PSI side.
findings.suggested_fix: Thread feature_names=feature_names through to the compute_categorical_drift_psi(...) call inside _compute_drift_invariant.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call compute_feature_distribution_drift(..., feature_names=<subset>) and assert every key in categorical_psi['per_feature'] is a member of the subset.

findings.summary: _binary_split_summary has no NaN handling (unlike the regression/multiclass/multilabel summarizers in the same file); a binary target split with missing labels is silently counted as all-negative, producing a misleading p_positive with no signal that labels were missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit NaN/missing count to _binary_split_summary's output and exclude NaN rows from the p_positive denominator (or report the missing fraction explicitly).
findings.meta_test_idea: Pass a binary target split that is 30% NaN and assert the summary surfaces the missing count rather than silently folding NaN into the negative bucket.

findings.summary: post_calibrate_model's calib_set_size parameter is documented as controlling the multi-output per-class isotonic path's slice size, but is never referenced anywhere in the function body -- a dead, misleading parameter.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire calib_set_size into the multi-output OOF-fallback slicing, or remove the parameter (with a deprecation warning) and correct the docstring.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call post_calibrate_model with two different calib_set_size values on the multi-output path and assert either the outputs differ or a DeprecationWarning fires.

findings.summary: The exploss builtin metric's pos_label = uniq[1] if uniq.shape[0] > 1 else uniq[-1] raises IndexError on empty y_true; iter_extra_metrics's narrow except tuple doesn't catch IndexError, so an empty-input report crashes the whole metrics pass instead of gracefully omitting exploss.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit empty-array guard in _exp returning nan, or add IndexError to iter_extra_metrics's caught-exception tuple.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call iter_extra_metrics with empty y_true/probs_NK/preds_NK and assert no crash occurs.

findings.summary: FieldGroupedMLPRegressor never validates that field_groups partitions X's columns exactly once, despite the docstring stating this contract; missing/duplicated indices are silently dropped or double-counted.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate in fit() that the union of all field index lists equals range(X.shape[1]) with no duplicates, raising ValueError naming the mismatch.
findings.meta_test_idea: Build field_groups covering only a subset of columns and assert fit() raises rather than silently training with reduced feature coverage.

findings.summary: build_keras_mlp(num_layers=N) builds N+1 hidden Dense layers (one unconditional block before the loop, plus N inside it), not N as the parameter name/docstring imply.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold the leading block into the range(num_layers) loop so the built count matches the parameter name.
findings.meta_test_idea: Assert build_keras_mlp(num_layers=k) produces exactly k hidden Dense layers of the configured width.

findings.summary: Recurrent wrapper's _factorize_cats_fit only factorizes explicitly-named cat_features columns, unlike the flat-MLP sibling which additionally auto-detects any remaining non-numeric column; an un-named categorical column crashes downstream instead of being handled gracefully.
findings.suggested_fix: Port the flat MLP's _auto non-numeric-column union (base/_base_fit_prep.py:71-72) into this method.
findings.meta_test_idea: Fit RecurrentClassifierWrapper with an un-named string column present and use_learnable_cat_embeddings=True; assert it factorizes instead of raising ValueError.

findings.summary: get_tracker_table's `model, task, _ = f.split("_")` assumes exactly 3 underscore-separated directory-name components; any real model/task name containing its own underscore breaks the unpack, aborting the whole tracker-table load.
findings.suggested_fix: Split with an explicit maxsplit anchored to the known trailing '_0' suffix (e.g. f.rsplit('_', 2)) or use a structured separator instead of relying on plain '_' splitting of caller-controlled names.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call get_tracker_table against a synthetic dirpath containing a name like 'my_model_cola_dev_0' (task with an embedded underscore) and assert a clear, named error or correct parsing rather than a bare unpacking ValueError.

findings.summary: _permutation_shapley recomputes score_fn(y, zeros) (the empty-coalition score) once per permutation even though it's a constant already computed once by the caller as v_empty, wasting ~1/n_models of the total score_fn call budget.
findings.suggested_fix: Thread v_empty (already computed in shapley_model_values) into _permutation_shapley/_msr_banzhaf instead of recomputing score_fn(y, zeros) inside the loop.
findings.meta_test_idea: AST/grep meta-test flagging any expression recomputed inside a loop bounded by an n_iterations/n_permutations-style parameter that is identical to an expression already computed once in the caller and not passed through.

findings.summary: _default_score_fn silently falls back to negative-RMSE (treating y as continuous) for any y whose cardinality isn't exactly 2, including degenerate single-class or integer-coded multiclass targets, with no warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise ValueError for cardinality > 2, or add an explicit multiclass-aware branch (e.g. macro-OVR AUC), instead of silently scoring RMSE-on-labels.
findings.meta_test_idea: Call shapley_model_values/shapley_blend with an integer-coded 3-class y and no explicit score_fn; assert it raises rather than returning a garbage score. Meta-test: grep default score_fn/metric_fn implementations branching on len(np.unique(y))==2 with no explicit else-raise for higher cardinality.

findings.summary: region_similarity_weights's documented 'rows summing to 1' invariant is silently violated when a query row's similarity to every region underflows exp(...) to exactly 0.0, returning an all-zero weight row instead of a sane fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: When row_sums <= 1e-12 for a row, fall back to uniform weights (1/n_regions) or route to the nearest region instead of leaving the row all-zero.
findings.meta_test_idea: Construct a query row with mean_dist far past the underflow threshold for the given similarity_scale and assert region_similarity_weights(...).sum(axis=1) is still 1.0.

findings.summary: np.nanmax on an all-NaN correlation row (from a constant/zero-variance prediction column) returns NaN, and NaN < correlation_threshold is always False, so a constant-prediction model is silently excluded from the diversity report instead of flagged.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly detect an all-NaN correlation row and treat it as max_corr = 0.0 with a logged warning, rather than letting NaN comparison semantics silently exclude the candidate.
findings.meta_test_idea: Include a constant-prediction model in oof_preds with a below-best individual score; assert it appears in (or is loudly, explicitly skipped from) diversity_ablation_report's output.

findings.summary: Neither hill_climb_ensemble nor _hill_climb_single_path validates that every oof_preds array shares y_true's shape, so a mismatched-shape array silently broadcasts into a wrong-shaped result instead of raising.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate all(p.shape == y.shape for p in preds) right after the np.asarray conversions, raising a ValueError naming the offending index.
findings.meta_test_idea: Pass one oof_preds entry with an extra trailing axis (n,1) alongside otherwise-valid (n,) arrays and assert a clear raise. Generalize as a scanner rule across constrained_weight_blend/geometric_weight_blend/dual_optimizer_weight_blend/adversarial_stochastic_blend, none of which shape-validate their stacked prediction arrays either.

findings.summary: minimax_ranking's models_scores.drop(model).max() is NaN for a 1-model leaderboard (drop empties the Series), making minimax_election() silently return an empty winner list instead of the one trivially-correct model.
findings.suggested_fix: Special-case n_models == 1 in minimax_ranking (return a 1-entry Series with a finite sentinel score) instead of letting .drop(model).max() degrade to NaN.
findings.meta_test_idea: Build a Leaderboard with exactly 1 model row and 2+ tasks, call minimax_election(), assert it returns [the_one_model]. Extend the existing F14 hand-computable election sweep to n_models=1 across every *_election method.

findings.summary: MLPRanker and ShortlistTransformerAdapter (both sklearn BaseEstimator subclasses) name their RNG param 'seed' instead of the sklearn-standard 'random_state' used by ~40 sibling BaseEstimator classes in the codebase.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to random_state with a deprecated seed alias for one release.
findings.meta_test_idea: Scan BaseEstimator __init__ params for RNG-like names (seed/rng/random_seed) differing from random_state when 3+ siblings in the same family already use random_state.

findings.summary: MLPRanker's epoch-count parameter is named n_estimators (docstring: 'epochs'; fed to max_epochs=self.n_estimators) while 4 sibling neural regressors in training/neural/ use n_epochs for the identical concept, and n_estimators already has a conflicting sklearn meaning (ensemble size).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename MLPRanker.n_estimators to n_epochs with a deprecated alias.
findings.meta_test_idea: Grep n_estimators on classes without a fitted estimators_/estimator_ list and cross-check docstring for 'epoch' language instead of 'tree'/'base learner'.

findings.summary: Full-suite worker count is computed as physical-cores/2, conflicting with the documented quarter-cores policy for pytest -n on this machine, motivated by a known Windows paging-file exhaustion failure mode under joblib fan-out.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the divisor from 2 to 4 to match the documented policy, or comment explaining a deliberate deviation.
findings.meta_test_idea: Scan scripts/CI for pytest-xdist worker-count formulas and assert the divisor matches the documented policy value.

findings.summary: Both mypy-full (whole-project) and mypy-full-manual (changed-files) run as blocking hooks on every commit, doubling mypy wall time paid per commit with the changed-files hook adding no coverage the whole-project superset doesn't already provide.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop mypy-full-manual once its cache-dir hazard is resolved, or document why both are needed simultaneously.
findings.meta_test_idea: Meta-test asserting at most one blocking hook per (tool, target-scope) pair in .pre-commit-config.yaml.

findings.summary: method='target_james_stein' is documented as variance-aware James-Stein shrinkage but its implementation (shrink = smoothing/(n_c+smoothing)) is algebraically identical to target_mean/target_m_estimate; it is not real James-Stein shrinkage and produces bit-identical output to target_mean given the same smoothing.
